pads.snippet: The purpose of TASPRI - Confirming is to support businesses and ventures led by women, specifically in the medium-sized enterprises segment, that need working capital to pay their suppliers. This is achieved through loans to women who have contracts that enable them to fulfill those obligations, which in turn ensures the repayment of the borrowed amount

pads.title: Visibility and dignity of women recyclers
pads.snippet: REDCicla is an initiative aimed at raising the visibility and dignity of women recyclers. It begins with the identification and mapping of women who recycle in the streets, disseminating their information so that neighbors, businesses, offices, institutions, ventures, companies, and government agencies can directly deliver their waste to them. Additionally, capacity-building for recyclers is conducted, along with the use of a mobile application, Redciclapp, that allows users to connect with them

pads.title: Technology and Employability for Women Builders
pads.snippet: A mobile application, called 'Women Builders,' available on Google Play, aims to connect the supply and demand for labor in the construction sector to promote greater participation of women in this predominantly male-dominated field. The initiative includes training in the use of digital technologies, including the use of the app. Initially, it works with 180 empowered women builders who have strengthened their skills in using and sustaining the application, thereby expanding their job opportunities in the sector

pads.title: http://reclama.bo/
pads.snippet:
http://reclama.bo/ offers legal assistance to women suffering from economic violence by addressing their demands for family assistance and labor rights. The business model used is the shared risk "No Win - No Pay," where legal fees are only charged when the case is won and there is a cash flow that allows for payment. Beneficiary women gain a deeper understanding of their legal rights in cases of economic violence and labor rights. They also develop skills to effectively file family assistance claims and labor grievances.

As a result, the beneficiary women experience an improvement in their well-being by obtaining justice and compensation for the economic violence suffered and violations of their labor rights. This enables them to recover emotionally and financially, contributing to the reduction of gender inequality and improving the quality of life for their families

pads.title: Companies that change lives
pads.snippet:
Companies That Change Lives supports high-impact businesses through a gender-focused blended financing mechanism. They invest in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the early stages and promote economic opportunities for women, while also contributing to climate change adaptation and mitigation.


The objectives are:

To support the development of financially underserved SMEs in the 'Missing Middle,' with special attention to gender justice and climate change.

To increase social impact by accessing new philanthropic and private capital aligned with impact goals.


To leverage Oxfam's expertise as a pioneer in the development sector and in promoting gender and climate justice in the impact investment sector.


Investment is made in women-led companies and in businesses that primarily support women throughout their value chain and have an impact on gender justice: women's leadership, decent work for women, inclusion of women in value chains, and transformative products and services for women.


In the climate context, sectors that support adaptation to climate change and climate change mitigation are included.

pads.title: ConexiónLab
pads.snippet:
ConexiónLab is an ecosystem of digital and innovative solutions implemented by the NGO Conexión, aimed at enhancing access to education and promoting job creation and entrepreneurship for young people in vulnerable situations.


ConexiónLab generates digital transformation in rural areas of Bolivia and Latin America by using digital solutions for training in digital skills, utilizing a digital platform, community connectivity models, and belonging to a digital community, JunteX.

ConexiónLab encourages the active participation of women in the initiative, promoting their leadership and digital entrepreneurship initiatives to immerse them in economic empowerment processes that improve their income and that of their region.

pads.title: SOS Digital Center
pads.snippet:
El Centro S.O.S Digital es una iniciativa de la sociedad civil, orientada a la prevención y el acompañamiento a víctimas de violencia digital, a partir de un enfoque de género y holístico. Entre las labores que realiza se encuentra:


1) Línea de acompañamiento e información de violencias digitales, que brinda apoyo emocional y asistencia técnica y legal de forma completamente anónima. 2) Talleres de capacitación de cuidados digitales y prevención de violencias digitales dirigidos a funcionarios públicos, estudiantes, profesores, padres/madres de familia, activistas y colectivos que lo requieran. 3) Auditorías de cuidado digital a organizaciones dedicadas a la protección de derechos humanos. 4) Desarrollo de guías y protocolos de seguridad digital y atención a casos de violencia digital.

pads.title: APPLIKATE: Digitalization, Management, and Financial Inclusion
pads.snippet: Mobile application aimed at facilitating financial management for micro-entrepreneurs and businesswomen. The application allows for the easy and intuitive recording of income and expenses (both business and personal), generating practical financial and business education. It helps organize financial information and enables the development of indicators and reports that assist in financial decision-making, as well as personalized advice through AI for a better understanding of their financial and business behavior. It also allows access to an Economic Support Fund (revolving fund) on preferential terms for those microenterprises that demonstrate good record-keeping practices

pads.title: Indigenous Women Applying Nature-Based Solution
pads.snippet: The Uru Uru Team’s solution is led by Indigenous women engaged in sustainable and efficient activities, applying Nature-Based Solutions such as the construction of floating rafts using Indigenous phytoremediation techniques to reduce pollution in Lake Uru Uru, combined with community gardens to generate food and income. This involves developing skills in environmental management and sustainable practices to strengthen phytoremediation techniques and community farming, fostering a behavioral shift toward greater environmental protection and sustainable practices within the community. Increased collaboration is also anticipated between Indigenous youth and other community members

pads.title: Women at the wheel
pads.snippet:
Women at the Wheel consists of a group of women with private cars who provide exclusive transportation services for women, children, and elderly people, as we prioritize the safety of passengers as well as the drivers.

The main advantage is that the drivers can manage their time and leave their homes to take pre-scheduled rides based on the contracts they handle each month, allowing them to budget their income. On the other hand, families receive support with caregiving tasks, especially in transporting their children or elderly adults.

pads.title: App Credit
pads.snippet:
App-Credit es una plataforma digital de bienestar financiero que empodera a mujeres emprendedoras en Latinoamérica, promoviendo su autonomía financiera y acceso a redes de apoyo duraderas. Con una oferta integral, App-Credit proporciona cursos virtuales con guía y asesoramiento personalizado, que cubren desde educación financiera y gestión empresarial hasta la estructuración de nuevos emprendimientos, adaptándose a las necesidades específicas de cada emprendedora.


La plataforma facilita el acceso a financiamiento mediante la creación de modelos de negocio y perfiles financieros sólidos, maximizando las oportunidades de las emprendedoras para obtener apoyo de instituciones financieras, fondos privados y otros mecanismos de financiamiento. Un componente clave es el módulo “Desafiando Barreras para Emprender,” un espacio diseñado para abordar los desafíos únicos que enfrentan las mujeres en el ámbito empresarial. Las coaches de App-Credit, capacitadas con un enfoque de género, brindan un acompañamiento adecuado y continuo.


Además, App-Credit fomenta el desarrollo de negocios comprometidos con la sostenibilidad, alentando prácticas responsables con el medio ambiente y la comunidad. Cada programa es evaluado mediante encuestas previas y posteriores, y cada graduada se convierte en miembro del Club App-Credit, lo que permite un acompañamiento a largo plazo.

pads.title: Connected
pads.snippet:
CONECTADAS is a space where women entrepreneurs and businesswomen can network with each other and with business service providers, while also acquiring new knowledge and/or tools alongside two experts and the business life experiences of two women entrepreneurs or businesswomen in each city where this space is implemented.


The methodology begins with a Speed Networking session, consisting of short 2-minute meetings among all participants of the event to establish contact networks. This is followed by training sessions led by experts, two of which are 30 minutes each. Next, there are meetings with suppliers (reverse fair) where businesswomen and entrepreneurs have the opportunity to meet various business service providers and connect with them. The event also features presentations from role models, where the guests share a bit about their business lives, and finally, the event concludes with a networking lunch.

pads.title: Legendary
pads.snippet:
Legendarias is a meeting space for women that seeks to highlight role models and learn from their knowledge and experiences. The space includes four businesswomen, entrepreneurs, or leaders from various fields, and a moderator. First, the guests present who they are, what they do, and their greatest mistakes and successes. Then, they move on to a live interview in which they collectively answer four questions: What brought them to where they are, what practical tool helps them on their path, what success means to them, and what skills an entrepreneur should have.


As a result, entrepreneurs begin to connect with local and national networks of women entrepreneurs/businesswomen, which allow them to access economic and management support for women-led micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MiPYMES) in La Paz, El Alto, Cochabamba, and Santa Cruz. The final outcome: improved socioeconomic conditions for women entrepreneurs.

pads.title: AIDA's Backpack
pads.snippet:
The "AIDA's Backpack" initiative addresses the challenges in providing comprehensive sexual education to adolescents and young people using a gamified approach to effectively convey critical topics such as teenage pregnancy, contraception, substance abuse, sexually transmitted infections, and gender-based violence. Its main objective is to empower young people to make informed and responsible decisions. The initiative targets adolescents and young people aged 13 to 20, promoting better decision-making in sexual health and, consequently, healthier sexual lives. This methodology includes a rights-based approach and focuses on gender and new masculinities.


The project also trained 80 youth leaders as peer educators, empowering them to actively participate in training and share knowledge about sexual health with their peers. This approach not only expands the project's reach but also fosters a sense of responsibility and leadership among young people.

The gamified content was developed in collaboration with health professionals, ensuring that the identified thematic priorities were effectively addressed. The solution includes activity planning tools and activity reporting models, providing a broader view of monthly progress.

The AIDA Backpack was recently distributed to 20 health centers in the Municipality of Oruro, and will be distributed to the 9 Platforms for Adolescents and Young People for the Prevention of Teenage Pregnancy, in coordination with the Youth Directorate of Viceminister of Equal Opportunities, covering the entire country.

pads.title: Off to the Market, I Won't Be Long: A Support Platform for Women Affected by Violence in Public Ma…
pads.snippet:
The initiative seeks to transform the San Antonio market in Sucre into a safe space for women who have experienced violence by creating a support platform among “caseras” (female vendors), sustained through economic ventures that leverage the market’s own potential. The program aims to reclaim the culturally female-dominated space of markets, using forums with legal and psychological specialists from feminist collectives to raise awareness on gender violence among the vendors. These forums also create a space for them to share their own experiences and build connections. The forums run alongside practical skills workshops, like embroidery and composting, inspired by the concept of 'learning by doing' from embroidery circles. The goal is for economic ventures to sustain the platform itself while supporting participants' economic independence.


The project has supported 24 vendors from the San Antonio market, who participated in gender discussions, unlearning violence, and learning the critical steps for supporting women affected by violence, all held within embroidery circles. The participating 'caseras' applied this knowledge by creating clothing for the Virgen de Guadalupe festival and the university parade, while also sharing their personal experiences with violence and their skepticism toward authorities.

In the second phase, the goal was to formalize the platform by strengthening the women’s leadership skills and establishing partnerships with feminist collectives to ensure continuous training and a referral network for legal and psychological support. This phase also included an environmental component, offering composting workshops to utilize organic waste from the market, with an eye toward generating resources to sustain the platform and support the vendors through composting modules within the market.

Immediate outcomes include increased awareness among participating 'caseras' on gender violence prevention, and their appropriation of the support platform within the market. Intermediate outcomes aim for the platform to formalize alliances with feminist collectives to continue training processes and offer specialized legal and psychological support. Ultimately, the platform is expected to generate resources for its sustainability, providing economic benefits to participants and creating a model that can be extended to other markets.

pads.title: Chacha Ventures:Promoting New Masculinities and Entrepreneurship Among Andean Indigenous Youth
pads.snippet:
"Chacha Entrepreneurs" ("Chacha" means man in aymara language) s an innovative development program for indigenous young men, aimed at promoting new masculinities and socio-emotional skills. The project is grounded in reducing violence, expanding access to opportunities, and fostering equity, with a proactive focus on engaging men from the community. It provides them with opportunities to connect with prominent figures in the Bolivian business sector and alumni of prestigious scholarships from the Spanish and U.S. embassies. Besides, it focuses on new masculinities, featuring discussions with leaders from diverse organizations and individuals representing various social and sexual identities. These experiences have been highly enriching for participants.


The program also offers mentorships to help men develop a business pitch, conduct market research, and access seed funding. By the end of the program, the indigenous young men involved gain greater awareness of their surroundings and explore a renewed vision of masculinity that emphasizes peace over conflict. They are creating solutions adaptable to markets, capable of launching triple-impact enterprises that also reclaim their indigenous identity. In doing so, they reshape the concept of 'chacha' or man within their communities, moving away from associations with violence.

pads.title: Redvers E-mobility: Converts Fuel Motor Bikes to Electric
pads.snippet: From fuel Boda Boda to E-Moto: Boda bodas are a lifeline for tens of millions of Ugandans, providing affordable and accessible transportation. However, at the same time, they also contribute significantly to air and noise pollution and operate within a challenging market environment where drivers struggle with high fuel costs and thus limited income. Redvers saw an opportunity to address these issues while simultaneously creating positive social and environmental impact. Our Solution. Electric motorcycles (e-motos) are offered through a unique lease-to-own model and a network of convenient battery-swapping stations. These converted e-motos are not only cost-effective and environmentally friendly but also rugged enough to handle Uganda's demanding roads. Drivers can lease these motorcycles with an affordable daily fee and complimentary maintenance, significantly boosting their income while transitioning to clean energy.

pads.title: Maisha: Malaria Drug from Indigenous herbs
pads.snippet: Joel Felix Ochom a third-year pharmacy student at Makerere University, narrowly survived becoming a malaria-death statistic at the age of 14. This experience sparked his passion to finding a permanent cure for the malaria disease. After joining Makerere University to pursue a Bachelor of Pharmacy, Joel convinced his friends, Valentine Muhoozi, Jimmy Kabuna, Robert Zziwa and Rita Ainembabazi formed a team to research on the different options of drugs for treating malaria.

pads.title: Composting for waste management in Villages around Nusantara Capital City
pads.snippet:
As part of the Empowering Rural Resilience through the Nusantara Green Village Initiative, UNDP Indonesia Accelerator Lab organized waste management training sessions for 40 residents in a rural area surrounding Nusantara, Indonesia's new capital city. The sessions covered both organic and non-organic waste management, focusing on practical techniques such as composting, maggot farming, and ecoenzyme production, alongside non-organic practices like creating ecobricks and upcycling materials. These methods aim to transform waste into valuable resources while fostering environmental stewardship.

The training emphasized the potential of organic waste to be repurposed into products like fertilizers and natural cleaning agents, while non-organic practices promoted resource reuse and innovation. To encourage immediate application, composting bags were distributed, equipping participants to begin composting at home and implement sustainable waste management practices in their daily lives.

This initiative not only addresses critical waste disposal challenges in rural communities but also empowers residents with innovative, resource-efficient skills. By fostering sustainable practices, it supports the broader vision of Nusantara as a resilient and environmentally responsible forest city.

pads.title: Ushahidi platform; open-source software tool designed to collect, visualize, and analyze crowdsour…
pads.snippet:
The Ushahidi platform is an open-source software tool designed to collect, visualize, and analyze crowdsourced data from multiple sources to create customizable maps and timelines, making it easy to track, organize, and present information. Its adaptability makes it valuable for applications such as disaster response, human rights monitoring, community engagement, and civic participation. The platform's strength lies in its ability to democratize data collection and empower communities to tell their own stories. 

The UNDP Indonesia Accelerator Lab, in collaboration with the National Land Agency’s project office (PMO Jabodetabekpunjur) and OpenStreetMap (OSM) Indonesia Association, utilised the Ushahidi Platform for the lake mapping initiative in the Jabodetabek area to assess the flood mitigation potential of natural and artificial lakes while promoting citizen participation in decision-making processes.

From March to July 2022, participatory data collection was conducted using open-source technologies, including OpenStreetMap satellite imagery and qualitative surveys. In total, data from 170 lakes in the Jabodetabek area were collected through a crowdsourcing platform, making the information publicly accessible.

pads.title: Prévention des pertes et gaspillages alimentaires grâce à la mouche soldat noire
pads.snippet:
Lauréate du Urban Innovation Challenge (UIC) de l'Accelerator Lab en 2021, FOKKALIS, une organisation de la société civile, s'efforce de changer le paradigme autour des déchets, de quelque chose qui est perçu comme n'ayant aucune valeur à quelque chose qui peut générer de nouveaux produits et être une ressource renouvelable. À cette fin, FOKKALIS a aidé les vendeurs du marché central de Kramat Jati, à Jakarta, à trier les restes de fruits et légumes en articles comestibles et non comestibles. Les articles comestibles ont ensuite été envoyés aux petites et moyennes entreprises (PME) pour être transformés en produits alimentaires destinés à la vente sur le marché. Dans le même temps, les déchets organiques qui ne sont plus propres à la consommation ont été transformés en granulés d'alimentation et en engrais pour l'agriculture urbaine par bioconversion via la mouche soldat noire. 

Au cours de la période de mise en œuvre, les PME ont transformé avec succès 80 kg de déchets alimentaires par jour en nouveaux produits. De plus, la collaboration avec la communauté de la bioconversion, qui impliquait le traitement des déchets organiques à l'aide de mouches soldats noires, a permis de recycler 8 tonnes de déchets alimentaires chaque mois. Ces résultats démontrent que la stratégie de gestion des déchets alimentaires par une approche sociale peut non seulement contribuer à réduire le gaspillage alimentaire, mais aussi créer des opportunités économiques et bénéficier aux communautés locales, ce qui suggère un potentiel d'application à grande échelle.

pads.title: Boat made of Bamboo and Jerry Cans
pads.snippet: Communities across Indonesian cities grapple with the issue of water-related disasters, especially flood, through various strategies. One of them involves the creation of boats made of bamboos and jerry cans. These boats are constructed and used by community members as a means of transportation, carrying people, equipment, and other items for daily needs during flood. A replica of this was showcased in a Solutions Mapping Festival organised by the Accelerator Lab team, which was attended by representatives from the Ministry of National Development Planning (Bappenas) and the Ministry of Education, Culture, Research, and Technology.

pads.title: Prayer Mats & Carpets from Plastic Waste
pads.snippet: While conducting an ethnographic study on flood management across seven cities, UNDP Indonesia Accelerator Lab team identified several products sold by local entrepreneurs. One of the highlights was a female entrepreneur who processes plastic waste into prayer mats and carpets. MSMEs in Indonesia have increasingly integrated waste-generated and environmentally-friendly products such as this, embracing the notion of circular economy.

pads.title: Guardianas y guardianes de las semillas
pads.snippet:
Esta iniciativa nace en Chacsinkín, Yucatán, después del huracán Isidoro que, en 2002, ocasionó la pérdida de las milpas y cultivos y, con ello, el riesgo de la pérdida de la seguridad alimentaria de la población en la Península de Yucatán. Con la intención de recuperar las semillas criollas de maíz y otros cultivos de la milpa, las comunidades y organizaciones locales como Misioneros AC y Ket Ximbal lanzaron la primera Feria de Intercambio de Semillas, para recuperar semillas y contar con la posibilidad de cosechar en el siguiente ciclo de producción.

Por más de 20 años, los Guardianes y las Guardianas de las Semillas se han consolidado como con colectivo de hombres y mujeres mayas que ha preservado 22 variedades de maíces criollos y otras semillas relevantes para la alimentación en el sur de México. Este logro se ha alcanzado a partir de mantener la continuidad de la siembra en las milpas, aprender técnicas de preservación y de intercambiar   constantemente experiencias y conocimientos sobre el manejo agroecológico. 

Asimismo, este colectivo se ha convertido en un tejedor de alianzas con otras regiones mayas en Chiapas y Guatemala, así como con la academia y sociedad civil aceptadas en conjuntar esfuerzos que promuevan la preservación de saberes ancestrales y el desarrollo de medidas fortalecedoras de los sistemas agroalimentarios. Estas acciones les han permitido lograr ser más resilientes a los embates del cambio climático, asegurando con ello la seguridad y autonomía alimentaria de las comunidades que siguen sembrando las variedades criollas.

pads.title: Rice, Barley and Crayfish Cultivation
pads.snippet: In Barbados, a local grassroots innovator is working on cultivating rice, barley and crayfish together, thus reducing the water required to grow those products that are typically imported. This contributes to greater food security and sustainability.

pads.title: Carnival Costume Recycling Service
pads.snippet: Recycling service focused on costume/clothing waste generated during the Caribbean carnival season.

pads.title: Clean Energy Home Loan
pads.snippet: The Clean Energy Home Loan is about rewarding people who are looking to do things like add solar panels, window glazing and insulation to the home, or even buy or build a planet-friendly, energy efficient home.

pads.title: Federal Subsidy for Efficient Buildings
pads.snippet: Operated by the German development bank KfW, a tool derivated from the Climate Action Programme 2030 aiming to promote building renovation across the country. The BEG combines existing programs to promote energy efficiency and renewable energies in the building sector and supports, among other things, the use of new heating systems, the optimization of existing heating systems, measures on the building envelope and the use of optimized system technology.

pads.title: Property Assessed Clean Energy Programs
pads.snippet:
An innovative mechanism for financing energy efficiency and renewable energy improvements on private property. PACE programs exist for Commercial properties and Residential properties. The unique characteristic of PACE assessments is that the assessment is attached to the property rather than an individual. 
The recent extension of this financing model to energy efficiency and renewable energy allows a property owner to implement improvements without a large up-front cash payment.

pads.title: The Green Deal
pads.snippet: A UK government policy initiative that gave homeowners, landlords and tenants the opportunity to pay for energy efficient home improvements through the savings on their energy bills from 2012 to 2015. At the heart of the Green Deal was the rule that savings on bills would exceed the cost of the work. By meeting this 'Golden Rule', consumers were able to receive energy savings without direct cost. Consumers then paid back the cost of such improvements through the expected savings in their energy bills.

pads.title: Canada Greener Homes Initiative
pads.snippet:
The initiative includes Oil to Heat Pump Affordability program, Canada Greener Homes Grant, and Canada Greener Homes Loan.
Oil to Heat Pump Affordability program: grants up-to-$10,000 (regardless of province), or up-to-$15,000 in participating provinces, plus a $250 bonus (in participating provinces only), to switch from oil heating to an eligible heat pump.
Canada Greener Homes Grant (for existing applicants): grants-up- to-$5,000 to get part of your costs back for eligible home retrofits, plus up to $600 additional grant toward the total costs of your pre and post retrofit EnerGuide home evaluations.
Canada Greener Homes Loan: up to $40,000, interest-free with a repayment term of 10 years. The Canada Greener Homes Loan offers interest-free financing to help Canadians make their homes more energy efficient and comfortable, at the same time to reduce air pollution.

pads.title: Congestion pricing
pads.snippet:
Congestion pricing attempts to reduce traffic and pollution by charging prices to drive in certain parts of a city. It has been done in London, Stockholm and Singapore.

From June 2024, the New York City's plan will be the nation's first, charging most drivers a $15 toll for entering much of Manhattan below 60th Street. Trucks would pay $24 or $36, depending on their size. Taxi fares would go up by $1.25, and Uber and Lyft fares by $2.50. Officials expect the plan will reduce traffic in one of the world's busiest commercial districts by 17% - similar to other cities with congestion pricing - while also raising money for public transportation.

pads.title: 30km/h Streets
pads.snippet: Campaign calling for limiting speeds to 30 km/h where people walk, live and play, as streets that promote safe walking and cycling can reduce car dependency and harmful vehicle emissions that contribute to climate change. Barcelona has been taking more steps to apply the 30 km/h limit in 75% of the city‚Äôs streets, including main roads.

pads.title: BreatheLife
pads.snippet:
The project combines public health and climate change expertise with guidance on implementing solutions to air pollution in support of global development goals.


It provides a platform for cities to share best practices, works with municipalities to expand monitoring efforts that can keep citizens informed and facilitate more sustainable urban development, builds demand for new solutions that are working and support municipalities in effectively implementing them in their own cities, and educates people about the burden air pollution poses to our health and our climate and provide meaningful ways to take action both locally and globally

pads.title: Breathe Warsaw
Project Learning Tree Canada
pads.snippet: Advance environmental education, forest literacy, and career pathways using trees and forests, to help develop students‚Äô awareness, knowledge, and appreciation of the environment, builds their skills and ability to make informed decisions, and encourages them to take personal responsibility for sustaining the environment and our quality of life that depends on it.

pads.title: Meat-Free Monday
pads.snippet: Ask residents to go meat-free for just one day a week, as one significant source of pollution is the release of greenhouse gases like methane and carbon dioxide during the process of animal farming. These gases are produced during the digestion process of livestock and are released into the atmosphere through manure storage and application. Consuming more plant-based foods greatly reduces emissions, ultimately leading to cleaner air.

pads.title: Street Lighting Sensory Network
pads.snippet: Carbon dioxide monitors inside the streets‚Äô smart lights, which can provide real-time information on the worst affected areas regarding air pollution, allowing for more effective strategies in combating pollution and letting residents know which areas of the city are at the most significant risk to their health.

pads.title: Pollution vacuum cleaners
pads.snippet: Giant vacuum cleaners placed on buildings to clean the surrounding air, which can eliminate 100% of fine particles and 95% of ultra-fine particles within a 984-foot radius (300 meters).

pads.title: AIR - INK
pads.snippet:
Ink products made by condensing carbon-based gaseous effluents generated by air pollution due to incomplete combustion of fossil fuels.
It was made by Graviky Labs and was funded via Kickstarter People have to connect the KAALINK device to their car exhaust pipe, and within 45 minutes of driving, they‚Äôll have one fluid ounce (30 ml) of ink. The captured pollutants are then purified in a lab and manufactured into usable ink.

pads.title: Smart Green ASEAN Cities
pads.snippet: An European Union (EU) funded programme implemented by UNCDF in partnership with the ASEAN Secretariat in Jakarta, Indonesia. It  promotes sustainable urbanization in ASEAN by investing in green and smart city solutions.

pads.title: Electric Ireland Superhomes
pads.snippet: As an obligated party under the Irish energy efficiency obligation scheme (EEOS), Electric Ireland has set up a one-stop shop that provides energy efficiency measures such as installing heat pumps or a whole house retrofit including a renewable energy air source heat pump, high-standard insulation, air-tightness and advanced ventilation for indoor air quality. To finance the services, energy-poor customers can access grants from the Sustainable Energy Authority of Ireland.

pads.title: Energy Efficiency Obligation Scheme
pads.snippet: An energy efficiency obligation scheme (EEOS) is one way for EU Member States to achieve annual energy savings that are legally mandated. Under an EEOS, obligated energy companies have to carry out energy efficiency measures that help final consumers improve energy efficiency. This may include for example improving the energy efficiency of buildings, early replacement of electric motors, and installing energy management systems. In the spirit of a just transition, a share of these measures must be directed to households vulnerable to energy poverty.

pads.title: La Programa National de Eficiencia Energétic (The National Energy Efficiency Program)
pads.snippet: The National Energy Efficiency Program for induction cooking and electric water heating in the residential sector consists of replacing liquified petroleum gas (LPG) stoves with electric induction stoves in Ecuador's residential sector, taking advantage of the availability of electricity generated mainly from renewable sources. The program involves long-term and low-interest loans for users for the purchase of electric stoves and a fixed number of free kilowatt hours monthly and subsidized electricity. The program has so far put induction stoves in 750,000 households in Ecuador. Swapping LPG for electricity from non-fossil sources promotes both reduced air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.

pads.title: Hire-purchase Solar Panels
pads.snippet: The hire-purchase business model for solar panels aims to provide households with off-grid access to affordable clean energy through solar panels. SolarNow is a solar company based in Uganda that previously sold, installed, and serviced high-quality modular solar home systems on a hire-purchase basis to mostly rural households and businesses. Customers were offered an affordable 12-month plan that typically involved a deposit on the system followed by 12 monthly installments, after which they own the system. SolarNow has now evolved into an energy solution provider supporting businesses as well as institutions in the Education, Healthcare, and Non-profit sectors.

pads.title: Affordable biogas plants
pads.snippet: To facilitate clean cooking, Grameen Shakti is a social enterprise that introduced its Biogas Program in 2005 offering the installment of plants that turn organic waste into biogas. Biogas is therefore a clean cooking fuel, the residue can be used as a high-quality fertilizer and it reduces pollution. Biogas is a popular solution in rural areas due to the low cost of set-up and the abundance of organic waste materials.  So far, the company has installed more than 36,000 biogas plants all over Bangladesh. Grameen Shakti offers a hybrid payment model that incorporates features of microfinance and an in-house credit model, resulting in a more affordable biogas plant.

pads.title: Pay-As-You-Go Solar
pads.snippet: Large upfront costs often deter clean energy use.  The Pay-As-You-Go (PAYG) approach to solar energy removes the upfront price barrier by allowing end users to pay in affordable amounts over time. A company essentially rents consumers a solar home system. Basic systems have enough power to charge phones and lights, and larger ones can power small appliances like radios or TVs. PAYG schemes use smart meters installed in households to monitor energy use and enable consumers to pay in smaller increments on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis using mobile banking platforms. Through this model,  access to energy in off-grid areas is improved, companies can minimize the cost of collections by automating the receipt of payments and remote rural customers get immediate access to basic electricity without having to take out a loan.

pads.title: Heat pump
pads.snippet: Heat pumps help improve air quality and reduce GHG emissions compared to conventional heating technologies. A heat pump uses technology similar to that found in an air conditioner. It extracts heat from a source, such as the surrounding air, geothermal energy stored in the ground, or nearby sources of water or waste heat from a factory. Because most of the heat is transferred rather than generated, heat pumps are far more efficient than conventional heating technologies such as boilers or electric heaters. Households with a heat pump also spend less on energy than those using a gas boiler. In addition, a large‚Äêscale switch to heat pumps can prevent other risks associated with fossil fuel combustion such as carbon monoxide from poorly serviced heating stoves and gas boilers.

pads.title: 15-minute city
pads.snippet: Initially proposed in 2016 by Carlos Moreno, the ‚Äú15-Minute City‚Äù is an urban model that allows everyone, in every neighbourhood, to meet most of their daily needs within a short walk or bike ride of their home. Among other objectives, it aims to reduce unnecessary and unwanted travel and promote a modal shift away from private vehicles, delivering all the rewards of green and healthy transport and cleaner air. Overall, the goal is that of building safer, more resilient, sustainable and inclusive cities, as depicted in the Sustainable Development Goal 11. The concept has been adopted by Barcelona, Bogot√°, Melbourne, Ottawa, Paris, and Shanghai.

pads.title: Smog-Reducing Roofs
pads.snippet: 3M has developed Smog-Reducing Granules that allow manufacturers to produce shingles or capsheets that help eliminate smog pollutants and improve air quality. Each home or building with Smog-Reducing shingles helps remove smog pollutants that come in contact with that roof. The nitrogen oxides in smog are converted into a nitrate salt solid which is a more plant usable form of nitrogen.  The roof on a typical home has the smog-fighting capacity of 2-3 trees with over 1 million trees worth of smog-fighting roofing installed so far.

pads.title: Regenerative Biofilter
pads.snippet: Green City Solutions, with its biotechnology that combines the capabilities of mosses with the latest Internet of Things technology, has developed the world's first regenerative biofilters which helps people in particularly polluted urban areas to get fresh air and thus more healthy and quality of life. Innovative natural systems are the ideal complement to established urban greening. Where trees have no room to root and the care of green strips fails, Green City Solutions‚Äô products offer a measurable and space-efficient improvement in quality of life and stay. The core product is an air filter and cooler based on moss. The biotechnology is energy-efficient, generates no excess waste, and is 99% recyclable.

pads.title: Building Suburban Bike Culture with Community Bike Hubs
pads.snippet: There is significant untapped potential for cycling in suburban neighborhoods. The Center for Active Transportation (TCAT) uses an innovative, evidence-based approach to incubating cycling in suburban communities through community bike hubs. Community bike hubs are spaces where people can learn more about cycling, meet other people who cycle, and go cycling together. They offer bike loans, bike mentorships, earn-your-bike programs, and guided rides, to encourage people to adopt cycling in areas where few people cycle. By addressing significant barriers in suburbs outside of infrastructure, the approach can accelerate cycling adoption and grow a cycling community. TCAT‚Äôs community bike hub approach is based on a four-step approach that other suburban communities can replicate: 1) find the neighborhood, 2) identify local barriers, 3) remove barriers and start cycling, and 4) keep cycling. In total, they have launched six community bike hubs in four jurisdictions (Peel Region, Scarborough, Markham, and Newmarket), each with positive results.

pads.title: Construction Emissions Tool
pads.snippet: Construction is a major source of air pollution in cities. The Construction Emissions Tool is an open-source tool that helps construction companies to plan, monitor, and manage their polluting emissions. The tool enables the measurement of emissions from non-road mobile machinery (NRMM) throughout the demolition and construction phases of a project. Crucially, this also helps commissioners, such as local authorities or landowners, to review progress against agreed targets for a specific site. Hence, developers, contractors, local authorities, and auditors can all use this tool made available by the organization Impact on Urban Health.

pads.title: School Streets
pads.snippet: School Streets is an initiative to transform the roads outside schools so that only pedestrians and cyclists can use them at school drop-off and pick-up times. This way, School Streets can help to improve poor air quality around schools where children are clustered at the start and end of the day. They also make it safer to walk, cycle, and scoot to school, creating a more pleasant environment and giving children a chance to get some exercise. As of July 2023, almost 600 School Streets were in place across London, with more on the way. The initiative is run by Mums for Lungs.

pads.title: Health and Pollution Action Plan
pads.snippet: The Global Alliance on Health and Pollution (GAHP) has supported 13 countries developing a Health and Pollution Action Plan (HPAP). The goal of each HPAP is to establish pollution as a policy priority and to define and advance concrete actions to reduce exposure to pollution and its related health impacts. GAHP works with national and regional governments by bringing together stakeholders in government, civil society, and the private sector to develop and implement the HPAPs. The HPAP process is flexible and tailored to the needs of each country, but generally includes five steps: Data Collection and Analysis, Setting health based priorities for action on pollution, Preparation of a draft Action Plan, Stakeholder consultation and Implementation.

pads.title: IKEA Better Air Now Initiative
pads.snippet: In India, the burning of rice straw, a rice harvest residue, is one of the major contributors to air pollution. The Better Air Now Initiative by IKEA aims to reduce air pollution in Northern India by turning rice straw into renewable materials and products like baskets, rugs, and bowls. This provides a viable alternative to open burning for farmers, and turns a waste product into a valuable resource, while simultaneously reducing air pollution. The long-term ambition for Better Air Now is to include other parts of India and to share the pilot model with other crop-burning regions.

pads.title: Business Air Pollutant Emission Assessment
pads.snippet: The Air Pollutant Emission Assessment guide enables businesses to create a global overview of their air pollution emissions along the value chain as a way to spur actions to reduce emissions. Enabling a baseline analysis of a company's global air pollution emissions is a crucial first step to setting the stage for mitigating action. It can also make it possible to undertake health or other impact assessment analyses. By using the guidance, IKEA has set a baseline. This will enable IKEA to study the impact of existing mitigation strategies and ways to increase ambition through air pollution-specific mitigation measures. The guidance makes it possible to set a baseline for air emissions, and the result will be presented in the annual IKEA sustainability report.

pads.title: Industrial pollution tax
pads.snippet: Introduced alongside two other green taxes in 2014, Chile has a tax for PM, NOx, and SO2 emissions from industrial sources and thermo-electric plants. The tax is set at a variable rate based on the environmental damage associated with emissions in different areas. Thus, the tax rate not only captures the estimated marginal damage of a ton of emission in a specific locality but signals to companies the most environmentally efficient geographic location in which to be based. The policy has proved very effective, raising significant revenue and PM levels dropping by approximately seven percent from the regulated industries. In addition, generators have agreed not to develop new coal-fired plants and to phase out existing ones.

pads.title: Mi parcela no se quema (My plot I do not burn)
pads.snippet: Mi parcela no se quema is a national information campaign and capacity-building program raising awareness on the negative impacts of stubble burning. Stubble burning is a significant source of air pollution and contributes to biodiversity loss, soil degradation, and wildfires. Workshops teach farmers to avoid agricultural burning and opt for alternative stubble management practices such as using the stubble as ground cover, feed for livestock, or compost and fertilizer use. New production systems based on conservation agriculture are also promoted, which include maintaining permanent soil coverage, minimum tillage, and crop diversification.

pads.title: Air quality around sensitive receivers
pads.snippet: The Netherland's Sensitive Receivers Decree (Besluit gevoelige bestemmingen (luchtkwaliteitseisen)) prohibits buildings designated as sensitive receivers from being built near provincial roads and motorways. Sensitive receivers include schools for primary and secondary education, buildings for childcare, nursing homes, and elderly care. Furthermore, such buildings can only be built or expanded if the limit values for air quality are not exceeded.

pads.title: Hoy No Circula (The No Drive Days Program)
pads.snippet: The program aims to prevent, minimize, and control the emission of pollutants from vehicles that circulate in the State of Mexico.  It implements partial driving restrictions determined by a vehicle's emission level classification. These classifications dictate the days when a vehicle is permitted to circulate. In times of heightened pollution, additional limitations are imposed in accordance with the severity of the environmental conditions.

pads.title: Paris 15-minute city
pads.snippet: Paris is turning the city into myriad neighborhoods where residents can find everything they need within a comfortable 15-minute walk or cycle from home. The city plans to install a cycle path on every street and bridge, increase office space and co-working hubs in neighborhoods that lack them, expand the uses of infrastructure and buildings outside standard hours, encourage people to use their local shops, and create small parks in school playgrounds that would be open to local people outside of school hours to combat the city‚Äôs lack of public green space.

pads.title: Center for No-till Agriculture
pads.snippet: The Center for No-till Farming (CTNF) provides farmers with access to community, knowledge and technical advice on no-till farmning and conservation agriculture. Activities include field-level demonstrations, community-based training events and peer-to-peer communication to share experiences and provide resources. No-till farming is planting crops on farmland year after year without tilling the soil. In conservation agriculture, not burning residues means that after harvest, farmers leave all the residues on the field to decompose and serve as nutrients for the soil.

pads.title: Röstånga energikooperativ (Röstånga energy community)
pads.snippet: Röstånga energy community is a group of neighbours that enables members to acquire their own photovoltaic systems, and other renewable and energy-efficient energy solutions, at an affordable price. They reduce costs by cutting out the middleman and handling planning, purchasing, assembly, installation, and commissioning within the cooperative's framework. At the same time, members contribute with their own time and skills.

pads.title: Energy Community Of Karditsa (Energeiakh Koinothta Karditsas Synpe, ESEK)
pads.snippet: The energy community operates a processing and standardization unit for residual biomass that comes from the regional unit of Karditsa (forest residues, agricultural residues, urban tree prunings, etc.) and turns it into pellets. The region has a significant potential for residual biomass flows originating from agricultural residues, wood processing industries, and municipalities, which can support the development of bioenergy. Members of the community are municipalities, small and medium-sized enterprises, associations (estimated 8%), and citizens.

pads.title: EH!CO!CHE - The Shared Electric Mobility Cooperative of Aragón
pads.snippet: EH!CO!CHE is a non-profit consumer cooperative that offers sustainable mobility solutions to its members through the use of shared electric cars. It provides a car-sharing service where the vehicle is purchased by the cooperative and rented to members. The cooperation is directed towards all of Aragon, including cities and towns, organizations, companies or associations, and all people willing to change the chip and want to have a car that belongs to as many members as possible.

pads.title: Santiago respira (Santiago Breaths)
pads.snippet: Firewood used to produce as much as 94 per cent of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) emissions in some Chilean cities. In 2014, the Government launched a programme in the centre-south region to replace 200,000 firewood heaters with more energy-efficient heaters such as new gas, paraffin or wood pellet-based heaters. This resulted in a reduction in emissions and improved indoor air quality.

pads.title: Stockholm Congestion Tax
pads.snippet: The congestion tax is charged during fixed hours for vehicles driving into and out of Stockholm city center. The amount varies, depending on the time when the vehicle passes the toll station. The purpose of the congestion tax is to reduce congestion and improve accessibility. Due to the reduced traffic, the measure also results in health benefits of reduced air pollution.

pads.title: Environmental Episode program
pads.snippet: The Chilean government's Environmental Episodes program employs short-term solutions to lessen the intensity and detrimental effects of poor air quality spikes on human health. This policy calls for declaring "Environmental Episodes" on days when exceptionally bad air quality is predicted. Such Episode notifications set off a series of official procedures and public alerts meant to enhance local air quality and promote avoidance behaviors among the general public. It has been demonstrated that the program lowers mortality rates among the elderly on the day of and in the days following the implementation of the episode, as well as ambient concentrations of particulate matter.

pads.title: Escola Respira (School Breaths)
pads.snippet: Escola Respira (School Breathes) is a municipal programme of initiatives for improving air quality in school environments such as awareness-raising actions among the entire school community. It revolves around four core areas: the urban space, classrooms, recreational spaces, and cross-cutting and educational aspects. The programme includes 2 lines of action for actively working with schools ‚Äì air quality eco-audits and awareness raising ‚Äì and 4 more lines of action, including promotion of green walls, increasing safety, sustainable mobility and urban model initiatives.

pads.title: Solar for All
pads.snippet: Solar for All is a New York State utility bill assistance program (financial support scheme). New York State is funding solar farms to benefit nearby homeowners and renters who may not be able to access solar (clean energy). Through Solar for All, vulnerable households prone to energy poverty can get the benefits of clean energy while lowering their energy costs.

pads.title: Barcelona Superblock
pads.snippet: A strategy for transforming public spaces throughout the city, under a new, healthier and fairer model that supports local relations. Traffic is restricted in strategic areas while active mobility, connection to public transport, recreational uses, green spaces, social cohesion and a green and innovative economy are promoted.

pads.title: Nanjing Green Towers (Nanjing Vertical Forest)
pads.snippet: Along the facades, 600 tall trees, 500 medium-sized trees (for a total amount of 1100 trees from 23 local species) and 2500 cascading plants and shrubs will cover a 6.000 sqm area. A real vertical forest that will help to regenerate local biodiversity, will provide a 25 tons of CO2 absorption each year and will produce about 60 kg of oxygen per day.

pads.title: Our Clean Air Kit project
pads.snippet: Supplying citizens with testing kits to learn more about the air quality in their local areas. The kits include a monitoring tube and an easy-to-follow guide, so concerned citizens can get accurate answers about the air they breathe.

pads.title: Clean Cookstove Project
pads.snippet: Project providing around 20,000 energy efficient and clean cookstoves for local communities. The clean cookstoves use less than half of the wood previously required, meaning that women and children have to spend less time collecting and chopping the wood, less money purchasing wood, and are breathing in smaller volumes of particulate matter.

pads.title: Mandragore Carbon Sink Tower
pads.snippet: A design based on the mandrake plant and packed with many innovative energy-saving and carbon-capture technologies and strategies. It uses the best passive heating and cooling techniques to condition the interior space. It incorporates as many natural materials as possible and a literal forest of plants and trees

pads.title: Anti-smog guns
pads.snippet: The guns work by spraying water vapor into the air, which absorbs the pollutants before falling to the ground like rain. the machine can help clear the dust and pollution particles from the environment and also reduce PM 10 and PM 2.5.

pads.title: CityTree
pads.snippet: A moss filter with integrated ventilation, an irrigation system and sensors to capture environmental data. The moss cultures literally eat particulate matter and nitrogen dioxide out of the air‚Äîoffsetting many tonnes of CO2 equivalents per year.

pads.title: Transportation Fund for Clean Air
pads.snippet:
Support bicycle, pedestrian, and other transportation projects that help clean the air by reducing motor vehicle emissions by dedicating approximately $800,000 annually to projects across the city. 
The revenue comes from a $4 per vehicle surcharge collected by the California DMV on motor vehicle registrations in the nine-county Bay Area region.

pads.title: Switch off Air Pollution: Дулаан шийдэл
pads.snippet:
A project aims to improve the situation by reducing coal consumption in the city‚Äôs ger district, as the use of coal for heating homes in these areas is the main source of the city‚Äôs air pollution.


The project's objectives include: (1) promoting sustainable consumption patterns and behaviours in the individual housing sector of Mongolia through energy efficiency advisory and financial intermediation; (2) reducing pollution in Ulaanbaatar‚Äôs Ger areas through improved energy efficiency in housing, awareness raising, technical training and technological support to MSMEs and households.

pads.title: Replace a gas stove with an electric stove
pads.snippet: If you are a Massachusetts resident, you might qualify for a $500 rebate from Mass Save on a swap this year from a gas to an induction stove.

pads.title: New energy vehicles
pads.snippet: Introduced a series of policies such as purchase subsidies, tax exemptions, charging infrastructure and exemptions from the lottery to promote the sale of new energy vehicles and reduce vehicle emissions.

pads.title: Winter Action Plan for Air Pollution Control
pads.snippet: Policy designed to control air pollution in the fall and winter seasons in two major cities, Beijing and Tianjin, and prefecture-level cities nearby.

pads.title: Ecological compensation mechanism（生态补偿机制）
pads.snippet:
Mechanism aiming to use economic leverage to mobilize the incentives of local governments at all levels to tackle pollution. Based on the year-on-year changes in ambient air quality in each county and district, implementing assessment rewards and penalties and ecological compensation.

The improvement of ambient air quality in municipalities is assessed on a quarterly basis centred on PM2.5, and the amount of eco-compensation funds received by each municipality is determined accordingly. Municipalities with deteriorating air quality are required to pay eco-compensation funds to the provincial level to compensate municipalities with improving air quality.

pads.title: Using nano-additives on buildings
pads.snippet:
Nano-additives are nano-particles added to another material to improve its properties. 
One of the most commonly used nano-additives is nano titanium dioxide or nano-TiO2. Nano-TiO2 molecules can absorb ultraviolet radiation from the sun to decompose organic molecules, microorganisms, and nitric oxide pollutants. The result of this decomposition is harmless molecules such as water (H2O) and carbon dioxide (CO2).

pads.title: Building anti-smog towers
pads.snippet: Buildings with the purpose of removing pollution particles by sucking in polluted air at the top and releasing clean air at the bottom. It can reduce PM2.5 (fine suspended particles) concentrations by between 10 and 19 per cent over an area of 10 square kilometres.

pads.title: Cloud-assisted mesh sensor network solution
pads.snippet: Technology for air pollution real-time data acquisition in public regions, fit for outdoor air pollution minoring applications.. It can be applied in various scales of outdoor air pollution monitoring deployments to meet the needs for improved cost-effectiveness, energy-saving, and adequate coverage.

pads.title: Photocatalytic concrete pavements
pads.snippet: Photocatalytic concrete pavements is to curb air pollution problem due to vehicle emissions. The past studies have shown that up to 35‚Äì40% of NOx concentration was reduced in the presence of photocatalytic concrete pavements.

pads.title: Emissions Trading Scheme
pads.snippet: Regulation for Carbon emissions trading and related activities in the National Carbon Emissions Trading Market, and allocating allowances (also known as permits) based on the plant‚Äôs generation output, with a different benchmark for each fuel and technology, to limit and reduce CO2 emissions in a cost-effective manner.

pads.title: Urban Innovative Actions
pads.snippet: Urban Innovative Actions is an initiative of the European Union that provides urban areas throughout Europe with resources to test new and unproven solutions to address urban challenges. The UIA funds innovative projects that can demonstrate a positive impact on urban development, focusing on themes such as sustainable urban mobility, energy transition, and urban poverty.

pads.title: Federal Transit Administration -  Low or No Emission Vehicle Program
pads.snippet: The FTA Low or No Emission Vehicle Program (Low-No) provides funding to state and local governmental authorities for the purchase or lease of zero-emission and low-emission transit buses and related equipment, as well as the construction or leasing of facilities to support these vehicles. This initiative aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve air quality in urban areas, supporting sustainable and environmentally friendly public transportation solutions.

pads.title: California Climate Investments
pads.snippet: California Climate Investments utilizes proceeds from the state's Cap-and-Trade program to fund projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions, strengthen the economy, and improve public health and the environment. It supports a wide range of initiatives across various sectors, aiming to create a sustainable and low-carbon future for California while prioritizing benefits for disadvantaged communities.

pads.title: New York City Clean Energy Fund
pads.snippet: The New York City Clean Energy Fund, managed by the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA), supports initiatives aimed at increasing energy efficiency, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and promoting the adoption of renewable energy technologies in New York City. The fund provides financial incentives and technical assistance to projects that contribute to the city's clean energy goals and climate resilience.

pads.title: Innovate UK–Sustainable Innovation Fund
pads.snippet: The Sustainable Innovation Fund by Innovate UK provides financial support to businesses across various sectors to develop innovative solutions that drive economic growth while reducing environmental impact. It aims to help companies adapt to the challenges posed by climate change, focusing on projects that promote sustainability, resource efficiency, and low-carbon technologies.

pads.title: The Climate Investment Funds (CIF)
pads.snippet: The initiative provide financing to developing and emerging countries to support large-scale projects that mitigate and adapt to climate change. The CIF operates through targeted programs, such as the Clean Technology Fund (CTF) and the Scaling Up Renewable Energy Program (SREP), which fund initiatives including renewable energy deployment, energy efficiency improvements, and sustainable transport systems.

pads.title: The C40 Cities Finance Facility
pads.snippet: The C40 Cities Finance Facility  supports cities in developing and emerging economies to prepare and implement climate mitigation and adaptation projects. It provides technical and financial assistance to help cities develop sustainable infrastructure projects, such as low-carbon public transport systems and renewable energy installations, contributing to significant reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and enhancing urban resilience.

pads.title: The BioUrban project
pads.snippet: The BioUrban project, developed by the Mexican startup BiomiTech, features artificial trees that utilize microalgae to improve air quality in urban environments. These artificial trees are designed to perform the air-purifying functions of a small forest, making them especially suitable for densely populated cities where planting large numbers of real trees isn't feasible

pads.title: The Beskol School Heating Project
pads.snippet: The Beskol School in Kazakhstan has implemented a UNDP-supported initiative featuring a biomass boiler, significantly reducing heating costs and cutting CO2 emissions. This project, part of a broader effort towards low-carbon development, not only saves the school approximately $5,000 annually but also reduces yearly CO2 emissions by around 900 tons. The initiative underscores a practical application of sustainable energy solutions in educational settings, enhancing environmental and economic sustainability.

pads.title: The "Investor Engagement in the Energy Efficiency Sector in Kazakhstan" project
pads.snippet: The project aims to advance the energy efficiency of buildings and infrastructure by attracting investments from private investors, banks, and international financial institutions. This initiative takes a notable place in efforts for transitioning Kazakhstan towards more sustainable energy use.

pads.title: Charging Eco Space
pads.snippet: The project in Kutaisi, supported by RICDOG and 350.org, involves installing energy-generating bicycles in public squares to power devices and promote renewable energy. This 6-month initiative also includes community events to enhance ecological culture and raise awareness about climate change impacts.

pads.title: 100% Renewable Energy Resource Transition in Kutaisi by 2050
pads.snippet: The project aims to transition Kutaisi City entirely to renewable energy by 2050. This comprehensive project includes strategies such as enhancing solar and wind energy capacities, improving energy efficiency in buildings, and integrating energy education in schools. It emphasizes community involvement.

pads.title: "Renewable Energy without the State" Festival / I Международный фестиваль «Возобновляемая энергети…
pads.snippet: The festival aims to promote and develop renewable energy projects independently of state support in urban areas and beyond. It focuses on sharing successful, economically viable projects in solar, geothermal, and biomass energy. The event encourages entrepreneurs and activists to explore sustainable energy innovations and offers discussions on practical applications and cooperation without government involvement.

pads.title: Forum "Zhashyl upGRADE" / Форум Жашыл upGRADE
pads.snippet:
The Forum aims to enhance urban sustainability through three main goals:

Educational Enhancement: Increasing citizen awareness about the importance and maintenance of urban greenery through ecological, biological, and legal education.


Collaborative Tools Development: Working with decision-makers to develop initiatives for preserving green spaces.


Community Consolidation: Building a unified network of organizations and individuals focused on the conservation of urban greenery, fostering stronger community involvement and resource sharing.


These objectives collectively promote sustainable urban development by emphasizing the preservation and importance of green spaces in Bishkek.

pads.title: The Quezon City interactive storybook project
pads.snippet: The project aims to educate children on climate action, enhancing awareness and participation in sustainability efforts. This initiative creatively presents the city's climate policies through accessible formats like braille and audiobooks, ensuring inclusivity.

pads.title: Low Emission Zones
pads.snippet: Milan's Low Emission Zones, "Area C" and "Area B," are initiatives to reduce vehicular emissions and promote sustainable urban mobility. These zones regulate vehicle entry based on emissions, with stricter controls over time aiming for a fossil-free city center by 2030.

pads.title: Raahgiri Day - a car-free days initiative
pads.snippet: Raahgiri Day is an urban movement in India aimed at promoting non-motorized transport by temporarily closing streets to vehicles and opening them up for people to engage in various activities. It emphasizes safe, inclusive, and sustainable urban mobility, encouraging walking, cycling, and community interaction.

pads.title: Menged Le Sewe ("Streets for People")–a car-free days initiative
pads.snippet: In Addis Ababa, the "Menged Le Sewe" initiative promotes sustainable urban mobility by organizing car-free days, encouraging activities like cycling and walking, and improving public spaces. This project involves local communities and government support to reshape urban transportation and enhance road safety and livability.

pads.title: Project on changing mobility habits
pads.snippet: City of Modena aims to shift urban mobility from private car use to more sustainable methods like cycling and walking by 2030. It was developed through a collaborative process involving a task force of citizens and technicians, enhancing the strategy with direct user input. This inclusive approach has already led to the creation of safer, quieter areas, pedestrian zones, bike lanes, and shelters in the city's historical center. The city continues to explore ways to further encourage public and electric transport use.

pads.title: AntiSmog–Net SAS
pads.snippet: The ANTISMOG project by Net Sas uses an innovative hydrogen-based technology to reduce emissions from combustion engines by up to 80%. This open-source technology enhances fuel combustion, leading to fewer emissions and improved engine efficiency.

pads.title: The Gecoair App
pads.snippet: A mobile application designed to help car drivers reduce the environmental impact of their journeys. It acts as a barometer of clean mobility by providing real-time feedback on emissions (CO2, NOx, fine particles, carbon monoxide) and offering guidance on eco-responsible driving practices. The app encourages the use of sustainable transport modes and has achieved significant engagement with over 40,000 downloads and 80 million km tracked, showing a potential 20% variation in CO2 emissions based on driving habits.

pads.title: The ADB's "Tackling Air Pollution in Bishkek": Waste Management Modernization
pads.snippet: This project aims to improve waste management practices to reduce the burning of solid waste, which contributes to air pollution.

pads.title: The ADB's "Tackling Air Pollution in Bishkek": Residential Heating Upgrade
pads.snippet: This initiative focuses on replacing traditional heating methods with more sustainable alternatives to reduce air pollution from residential heating.

pads.title: QYZPU's Project On Plant Cultivation
pads.snippet: The project by scientists from QYZPU in Almaty, Kazakhstan, focuses on improving urban air quality through the cultivation of plants that can absorb harmful substances. This green initiative will be implemented in densely populated areas of Almaty after coordinating with local authorities.

pads.title: Envinity Group's Outdoor Air Cleaner
pads.snippet: The Giant Dutch Vacuum Cleaner, developed by Envinity Group, is designed to significantly improve air quality by filtering out fine particulate matter from the urban atmosphere. It can clean more than 280,000 cubic feet of air per hour, capturing 100% of fine particles and 95% of ultra-fine particles, which are known to be harmful to human health.

pads.title: Smog Eating Billboard project
pads.snippet: The Smog Eating Billboard project in Monterrey, developed by UDEM students with Daan Roosegaarde, applies photocatalytic coatings to billboards to purify urban air. This innovative approach cleans the air equivalent to the work of 30 trees every six hours and has the potential to significantly reduce air pollution in densely populated and visually polluted urban environments.

pads.title: Smog Free Project: Smog Free Tower
pads.snippet: The Smog Free Project, led by Daan Roosegaarde, is an innovative environmental initiative that includes the Smog Free Tower, the world's first smog vacuum cleaner. This project aims to improve urban air quality by creating zones of clean air in public spaces, and it engages communities through educational campaigns and collaborative design workshops.

pads.title: The "Clean Air" federal project (Федеральный проект "Чистый Воздух")
pads.snippet: The "Clean Air" project, part of Russia's national ecological initiatives, aims to significantly reduce air pollution in the largest urban areas by enhancing federal and regional regulations and technological upgrades in industrial centres of the country (tagets a number of cities and regions that host the pollution-intensive production facilities). Incluses such steps as modernization of industrial enterprises and existing boiler houses, conversion of heating in private households from coal to more environmentally friendly fuel, launch of public transport using electricity and NGV fuel.

pads.title: The Climate Action Tracker
pads.snippet: The Climate Action Tracker (CAT) is an independent scientific tool that assesses government climate actions against the Paris Agreement's targets. It evaluates national climate mitigation efforts, predicts future emissions impacts, and identifies emissions gaps to guide global warming mitigation strategies.

pads.title: City carbon networks
pads.snippet: The study on city carbon networks assesses how urban consumption impacts hinterland emissions and guides investment and trading strategies for carbon reduction. By mapping the flow of emissions between cities, it highlights how targeted carbon trading can enhance mitigation efforts and accelerate progress towards carbon neutrality. This approach aims to refine global and local strategies to reduce carbon emissions effectively.

pads.title: Climate Budget Tagging (CBT)
pads.snippet: Climate Budget Tagging (CBT) is a financial management tool designed to help governments track and optimize their climate-related expenditures within public budgets. It aims to enhance the transparency and efficiency of climate finance and is a crucial component in integrating climate change considerations into broader fiscal policies and strategies.

pads.title: Green City Bond
pads.snippet: Green City Bonds provide a financial mechanism for cities to fund sustainable infrastructure projects.  The approach allows cities to raise capital for projects that improve environmental sustainability and resilience, such as renewable energy installations and energy-efficient building upgrades.

pads.title: Climate Budgets
pads.snippet: The concept of climate budgets focuses on integrating climate action into the financial planning of cities. By allocating specific portions of the budget to combat climate change, cities can systematically address environmental targets in line with their economic strategies.

pads.title: eTrash2Cash
pads.snippet: The project incentivizes recycling by buying waste from the public, focusing on transforming it into recyclable products and organic compost. This initiative not only aims to reduce environmental pollution but also offers financial benefits to low-income earners, promoting sustainable waste management practices.

pads.title: Jelbi
pads.snippet: Jelbi aims to reduce car traffic in metropolitan areas by providing a seamless mobility service. Launched by Berlin's public transportation agency, BVG, and developed by Trafi, a Lithuanian startup, Jelbi merges public transport, shared vehicles, and on-demand services into one app. With over 25 transportation partners, Jelbi enhances urban liveability by improving air quality and reducing CO2 emissions through decreased car use. The service also plans to introduce dynamic pricing and uses data to aid city planning, such as preventing traffic jams and creating new bike lanes.

pads.title: Airly, air sensors
pads.snippet: Airly addresses air pollution through a network of sensors providing real-time air quality data. This initiative empowers individuals, communities, and policymakers with actionable insights to combat pollution and enhance public health.

pads.title: The Carbonlites project
pads.snippet: The Bangalore-based startup's initiative, Carbonlites, converts organic waste into biogas, effectively turning garbage into a renewable energy source. This innovative approach not only reduces the volume of waste in landfills but also produces a cleaner alternative to liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and generates organic fertilizer, addressing waste management and energy challenges simultaneously.

pads.title: Organic Waste to Biogas: Biomethanisation Unit
pads.snippet: Solution for solid-state batch anaerobic digestion for organic waste, turning it into renewable energy and compost. This collaboration, pioneering in Brazil, embodies a Nature-based Solution (NbS) and Circular Economy, aiming for significant CO2 reduction by diverting waste from landfills. The project supports urban agriculture and reforestation, enhancing soil, fostering biodiversity, and improving food security, aligning with Rio's Climate Action Plan to reduce GHG emissions and advance zero-waste governance.

pads.title: Urban Micro-Lungs Initiative
pads.snippet: The Urban Micro-Lungs (UML) initiative in East Amman, Jordan, funded by the German Federal Ministry and implemented by GIZ in partnership with local entities, introduces urban micro-forests using the Miyawaki Method to combat urban densification and climate change effects. This green infrastructure project enhances air quality, reduces water runoff, and supports local biodiversity, all while involving the community in beautification efforts. It serves as a replicable model for urban greening, emphasizing low-maintenance, drought-tolerant native plants and participatory approaches for sustainable urban development.

pads.title: Smarter Cities Partnership, New Weatherization Program - Home Uplift
pads.snippet: In Knoxville, Tennessee, weatherization programs initiated in partnership with local and national organizations have significantly improved the energy efficiency of homes, especially for low-to-moderate income families. Since 2015, over 1,800 households have benefitted from investments exceeding $17 million, aimed at reducing utility bills and enhancing indoor air quality. These initiatives not only help residents save on energy costs but also contribute to reducing community carbon emissions and improving public health.

pads.title: Urban Forest Strategy
pads.snippet: The Urban Forest Strategy aims to expand Melbourne's tree canopy from 22% to 40% by 2040, enhance biodiversity, and ensure species diversity by limiting the proportion of any single tree species, genus, and family. It focuses on improving vegetation health, soil moisture, and biodiversity. Community engagement and consultation are key components of the strategy, ensuring the city's green efforts are inclusive and informed by residents' input.

pads.title: Community Air Monitoring Programs
pads.snippet: Clean Air Now: A global network of CSOs working to improve air quality around the world. They provide resources, training materials, and support for community air monitoring programs

pads.title: مبادرات النقل العام المستدام / Sustainable Public Transportation Initiatives
pads.snippet:
Initiatives that promote sustainable public transportation in the Arab region. These initiatives focus on improving the efficiency, affordability, and accessibility of public transportation systems, with the ultimate goal of reducing air pollution and promoting sustainable urban mobility.

Expanding Public Transportation Networks: Investments in expanding bus rapid transit (BRT) systems, light rail networks, and metro lines in major cities.


Improving Service Quality: Increasing the frequency, reliability, and safety of public transportation services.


Promoting Integrated Ticketing Systems: Implementing smart card systems that allow passengers to seamlessly transfer between different modes of public transport.


Enhancing Infrastructure for Non-Motorized Transport: Developing dedicated cycling lanes and pedestrian walkways to encourage walking and cycling for short trips.


Encouraging Ridership: Public awareness campaigns highlighting the benefits of using public transportation, along with potential fare subsidies or loyalty programs.

pads.title: مبادرة المدارس البيئية\ الخضراء / Eco-Schools Initiative
pads.snippet:
The Eco-Schools Initiative is an international program that empowers students to become active participants in creating sustainable schools and communities. It encourages schools to integrate environmental education into the curriculum and implement environmentally friendly practices throughout their operations.

The program focuses on seven key environmental themes: Water, Energy, Waste, Biodiversity, Health and Well-being, Climate Change, Food
