Schools participating in the Eco-Schools Initiative follow a seven-step process that guides them through planning, taking action, monitoring progress, and achieving accreditation.

pads.title: Air Quality Monitoring and Forecasting for Informed Decision-Making
pads.snippet:
Effective air quality management relies on a combination of air quality monitoring and forecasting systems.
Monitoring: Regularly collecting air quality data through strategically placed monitoring stations is crucial. These stations measure concentrations of various pollutants like particulate matter (PM), ozone, and nitrogen oxides.
Forecasting: Using air quality models and meteorological data, forecasts can predict future air quality conditions. This allows for proactive measures to be taken.
This combined approach provides valuable information for:
Public health advisories: Issuing warnings to vulnerable populations when air quality reaches unhealthy levels.
Regulatory enforcement: Tracking compliance with air quality standards and taking necessary actions.
Emission reduction strategies: Identifying sources of air pollution and informing policies to control emissions.

pads.title: Industrial Process Fuel Switching (considering technical and economic feasibility)
pads.snippet:
Industrial fuel switching involves replacing existing fossil fuels used in industrial processes with cleaner alternatives. This can significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions, air pollutants, and other environmental impacts associated with industrial activities. However, the feasibility of fuel switching depends on several factors:
Technical Compatibility: The new fuel must be compatible with existing industrial equipment and processes. Modifications might be necessary for some fuel switches.
Economic Considerations: The cost of the new fuel, potential infrastructure upgrades, and overall operational efficiency changes need to be assessed. Switching to a cleaner fuel should ideally be economically viable in the long term.
Fuel Availability: Reliable access to the new fuel source in sufficient quantities is crucial for successful implementation.

pads.title: Urban Heat Island Mitigation Strategies (combining various approaches)
pads.snippet:
Urban Heat Island (UHI) mitigation strategies encompass a variety of approaches to reduce heat absorption and promote cooling effects in urban areas. Here are some key strategies:
-Increasing Vegetation and Green Space: Trees, shrubs, and other vegetation provide shade, absorb heat, and release cooling moisture through transpiration. This can involve planting trees along streets, creating green roofs, and establishing urban parks.
-Using Cool Materials for Roofs and Pavements: Replacing traditional dark roofs and pavements with lighter, reflective materials reduces heat absorption and lowers surface temperatures. This can involve using reflective coatings or installing green roofs.
-Promoting Smart Growth Practices: Urban planning that incorporates green infrastructure, encourages compact development, and minimizes heat-trapping concrete expanses can significantly reduce the urban heat island effect.
-Urban Water Features: Fountains, water streams, and strategically placed ponds can provide evaporative cooling and create a more comfortable microclimate.

pads.title: Improved Cooking Stoves and Fuel Distribution Programs

tags.name: Cleaner Energy (indirectly through promoting cleaner fuels)

pads.snippet:
This solution promotes the transition from traditional cooking stoves (often burning biomass like firewood or charcoal) to improved cooking stoves and cleaner fuels. Improved cooking stoves offer several benefits: Increased efficiency, reducing fuel consumption and associated emissions; Reduced smoke and harmful pollutants released during cooking, improving indoor air quality and health; and Potential for using cleaner burning fuels like biogas or ethanol.
Effective programs often combine stove distribution with: Fuel availability: Ensuring access to cleaner fuels for the new stoves; Education and behavior change: Encouraging proper use and maintenance of the new stoves; and Financing mechanisms: Making improved stoves affordable for low-income households.

pads.title: Indoor Air Quality Regulations (National/Regional)
pads.snippet: Specific regulations for indoor air quality (IAQ) can be established at the national or regional level. These regulations set acceptable indoor air quality levels for pollutants and may outline monitoring, control measures, and enforcement mechanisms.

pads.title: Indoor Air Quality Management (Monitoring)
pads.snippet: Regularly monitoring indoor air quality is crucial for identifying and addressing potential issues. Monitoring practices can involve using sensors, conducting inspections, and analyzing air samples for various pollutants.

pads.title: Improved Public Transportation Systems
pads.snippet: This solution encompasses a variety of strategies to enhance public transportation infrastructure and services. It can involve expanding networks (buses, trains, trams, etc.), increasing frequency and reliability, improving accessibility for people with disabilities, integrating different modes of transport, and implementing fare structures that encourage ridership. Ultimately, improved public transportation systems aim to provide a more attractive and convenient alternative to private vehicles.

pads.title: Sustainable Biomass Energy
pads.snippet: Biomass energy refers to the generation of electricity or heat from organic matter like wood, crops, or agricultural residues. "Sustainable Biomass Energy" emphasizes practices that ensure the long-term viability of biomass resources, minimize environmental impacts, and promote positive air quality outcomes. This can involve using certified sources, maintaining forest health, utilizing efficient conversion technologies, and implementing emission control measures.

pads.title: Waste-to-Energy (WtE) Plants
pads.snippet: Waste-to-Energy (WtE) plants are facilities that burn municipal solid waste (MSW) to generate electricity or heat. This process reduces landfill waste volume and diverts it from landfills. The generated electricity can be fed into the power grid, while heat can be used for district heating systems.

pads.title: Precision Agriculture
pads.snippet: An approach to farming that uses technology and data to improve decision-making for crop management. It involves gathering information about soil conditions, crop health, and other factors to optimize resource use (water, fertilizer, pesticides) and ultimately increase agricultural productivity, sustainability, and contribute to improved air quality.

pads.title: Industrial Emission Standards
pads.snippet: Regulations that set limits on the amount of air pollutants that industrial facilities can release into the atmosphere. These standards aim to protect public health and the environment by controlling emissions from various industrial processes.

pads.title: Ultra-Low Emission Zone (ULEZ)
pads.snippet: A stricter variation of the Low-Emission Zone (LEZ), the Ultra-Low Emission Zone (ULEZ) enforces even more stringent emission standards for vehicles entering the designated urban area. This aims to significantly reduce air pollution from vehicle traffic.

pads.title: Low-Emission Zone (LEZ)
pads.snippet: This solution establishes a designated urban area where vehicles must meet a minimum emission standard to enter. The LEZ aims to discourage high-polluting vehicles and improve air quality within the zone.

pads.title: Public Awareness Campaign on Air Quality
pads.snippet: Educational campaigns designed to raise public awareness about air quality issues, their health impacts, and potential solutions.

pads.title: Indoor Air Quality Management Program for Schools
pads.snippet: This program provides a comprehensive framework for schools to identify, prevent, and address indoor air quality (IAQ) issues. It equips stakeholders with resources, guidance, and tools to create healthy learning environments.

pads.title: Indoor Air Quality Improvement Program
pads.snippet: A comprehensive program that combines various strategies to improve indoor air quality in homes, schools, workplaces, and other buildings.

pads.title: Protected Bike Lane Network Expansion
pads.snippet: This solution focuses on expanding a network of protected bike lanes, physically separated from traffic, to encourage cycling as a safe and viable transportation option.

pads.title: One Million Trees Movement (Urban Tree Planting Program)
pads.snippet: A nationwide effort in Singapore to plant one million more trees across the country over 10 years, increasing the total number of trees to over 8 million. The program focuses on planting trees in streetscapes, parks, gardens, nature reserves, and industrial estates.

pads.title: Regulations on Solid Fuels
pads.snippet: Regulations may set standards for cleaner burning solid fuels or restrict the burning of solid fuels in specific areas.

pads.title: Phase-out of Traditional Coal
pads.snippet: A gradual ban on the sale and use of traditional coal for domestic heating or industrial purposes.

pads.title: Community Air Monitoring Network
pads.snippet: A network of low-cost air quality sensors deployed by community members to collect and share real-time air quality data. Programs may involve citizen science training, data analysis tools, and collaboration with environmental agencies.

pads.title: School Bike-Sharing Program
pads.snippet: Schools partner with organizations to implement bike-sharing programs that provide students with access to bicycles for commuting, recreation, or educational purposes. Programs may involve secure bike storage, helmet use promotion, and basic bike maintenance education.

pads.title: Green Roof Incentive Program and Bylaw
pads.snippet: The City of Toronto implemented a combined approach to promote green roofs. The Green Roof Bylaw mandates green roofs on new developments exceeding a certain size, while the Eco-Roof Incentive Program provides financial incentives to property owners for installing green roofs on existing buildings.

pads.title: Commute Trip Reduction Program
pads.snippet: Programs that encourage employees to choose alternatives to single-occupancy vehicles for commuting, such as carpooling, vanpooling, biking, walking, or using public transportation. Programs may include awareness campaigns, employer incentives (parking cash-out, transit subsidies), and financial benefits through tax breaks.

pads.title: Zero-Emission Bus Rollout Plan
pads.snippet: Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) is developing a plan to convert its entire bus fleet to zero-emission buses (ZEBs) by 2040, prioritizing disadvantaged communities.

pads.title: Wood Stove Filter
pads.snippet:
The Exodraft ESP particle filter is designed to filter out hazardous and ultrafine particles from the flue gas of your wood-burning stove or fireplace.





The Exodraft ESP particle filter comes with a self-cleaning feature and catalytic-like technology. PM2,5

pads.title: Fugitive Dust Control in Construction Sites
pads.snippet: Using the FOG Canons/Sprays for weting the surface in construction sites/ demolition sites  in order to reduce the PM10. The aim of this solution is to reduce the PM10 and other particles to spread in the air.

pads.title: BCA Green Mark
pads.snippet: A green building rating system that promotes sustainable design and construction practices, including Passive Cooling System measures

pads.title: DWP5C project phase 2 - Development of Material Recovery Facility (MRF)
pads.snippet: UNDP has worked with Binh Dinh Environment Company in Quy Nhon city, Binh Dinh province to build up the MRF model, including technical designs, construction of the MRF’s warehouse and development of a network from both formal and informal sector to collect plastic wastes for MRF. This provided diverse benefits to business sector, local community and the environment. The capacity of MRF is 2-4 tons per day of plastic waste collected from domestic sources of the city. Through the MRF, plastic wastes are segregated by types, removed labels of bottles, baled and be ready to be sold to recyclers to turn them into new production chain as input materials. PET and HPDE are occupied main volume of the MRF’s output, which will be sold to Duy Tan Recycling Company, through an Agreement Principle with the MRF’s operator. To kick off the collection of plastic waste from domestic sources in the city, a MRF Fund has been established and collected 67 tons of plastic wastes, within 6 months, from informal sector and from the central landfill of the city.

pads.title: SEDAYA Community Empowerment Hub: Micro Equity Financing to Support Poverty Graduation through Ent…
pads.snippet:
Following a series of co-creation through participatory Focus Group Discussions (pFGDs) with People in Need of Social Welfare Services (PPKS) in urban Jakarta as well as solutions mapping consultation with stakeholders, UNDP Indonesia Accelerator Lab is developing SEDAYA - a community empowerment hub, with the following objectives:

1. Provide entrepreneurship training and business sustainability mentoring to PENA (Pahlawan Ekonomi Nusantara/Indonesian Economic Hero) graduates and other vulnerable micro enterprises in Jakarta.

2. Conduct Business and Risk Profile Assessment to selected PENA graduates, in order to examine their potential to access additional micro equity funding from social investors.

3. Foster collaboration and partnerships among key public and private stakeholders.

These objectives are intended to achieve two main outcomes:

1. Improved entrepreneurial skills of training participants to stay above the poverty line

2. Integration of lessons learned into the government’s poverty graduation strategy

This initiative offers a financing solution in the form of micro equity: an innovative financing mechanism that facilitates investments to strengthen business sustainability of emerging enterprises, with a Sharia-compliance profit sharing mechanism between the investors and micro enterprises.  

Elements of this pilot initiative will be tailored to help PENA graduates grow and sustain their businesses, while also equipping other PPKS who have not been reached through government programmes with the necessary skills and information to start their own businesses. The training modules and profile assessment will be conducted in collaboration with the Ministry of Social Affairs (MoSA), the Office of Social Affairs of DKI Jakarta (Dinsos DKI Jakarta), and Sub-National Development Planning Agency of DKI Jakarta (Bappeda DKI Jakarta).

pads.title: Hydropanel for condensing drinking water
pads.snippet:
The SOURCE® Hydropanel is a technology that incorporates multiple patented inventions alongside proprietary trade secrets, making it a one-of-a-kind renewable water technology that uses the power of the sun to extract clean, pollutant-free drinking water from the air. Collected water is then mineralized for optimal composition and taste, making high-quality drinking water a readily available resource.

A hydropanel is like a solar panel, but instead of creating energy, it creates clean, safe drinking water without electric hookups or infrastructure, nearly anywhere.

pads.title: Celal-Mex, pineapple pulp for paper and textiles
pads.snippet:
Mexico generates 6.3 million tons of pineapple waste annually, yet 705 of this waste is cellulose which can serve as a sustainable substitute for traditional cellulose. The green chemistry process of Celal-Mex uses 66% less water and chemicals than traditional cellulose production. 

Celal-Mex is a biotechnology initiative focused on the development of sustainable raw materials from agricultural waste in the form of cellulose and starch for industrial marketing.  Their objective is to take advantage of agricultural waste and give a second use to the byproducts of the field to develop sustainable and competitive alternatives to conventional polymers.

pads.title: Bioway
pads.snippet: BioWay is an application for mobile devices that supports the reinforcement of a strategy in the treatment, processing and management of these various wastes by connecting waste producers and collectors. Aiming for a virtuous circle, the person who wishes to discard the packaging of their products, committed to the environment, registers in the application so that they are considered part of the project and receive the information you need to contribute to good waste management. On the other hand, the app's collector-users  analyze the information received, to generate a strategy for collecting the waste that is generated by the registered people.

pads.title: Solar-powered floating pump system
pads.snippet:
In the Chullpia lagoon, in the Ocuviri district in Puno, the community implemented an irrigation system that works with solar energy to pump, from a boat, the water necessary for its productive activities. Its capacity for innovation and resilience contributes to having water in dry seasons.

En la laguna de Chullpia, en el distrito de Ocuviri, en Puno, la comunidad implementó un sistema de riego que

funciona con energía solar para bombear, desde un bote, el agua necesaria para sus actividades productivas. Su capacidad de innovación y resiliencia contribuye a contar con agua en las temporadas de sequía.

pads.title: "Telewer" Solution de télémédecine
pads.snippet:
Au Sénégal, l'accès à la santé est très limité dans la plupart des régions, notamment dans les zones frontales. A Sédhiou, Matam et Tambacounda, les distances entre un poste de santé et un hôpital de référence varient de 43 à 60 km. Aussi, si en Afrique l'accès à un personnel de santé est de 1 médecin pour 5000 habitants, au Sénégal, les chiffres sont 1 pour 14000 habitants. 

Avec sa solution "TeleWer" Senvital propose des services de télémédecine par le biais d'une plateforme numérique réunissant les professionnels de la santé avec ces populations déshéritées.et des personnes ayant un accès limité aux infrastructures de santé.

tags.name: New national standard in stormwater design

pads.snippet: Detroit-based Parjana Distribution LLC is partnering with Lawrence Technological University (LTU) on a pilot project that involves testing a new stormwater drainage system for parking lots that is expected to significantly reduce stormwater runoff volumes. The technology, named energy-passive groundwater recharge products (EGRPs), includes 31.75mm-diameter hydrophobic, polyethylene tubes composed of five chambers and open channels along edges. Designed to handle up to an inch of rain (25mm) during a 24- hour period, EGRPs facilitate underground water recharge by balancing soil moisture and promoting movement of water between horizontal soil layers.EGRP can be used to improve drainage to infiltrate standing water, manage soil moisture to protect underground infrastructure, or recharge water depleted soils to replenish wells and rejuvenate rivers.

pads.title: La Caja Verde
pads.snippet:
To take an example, we will analyze the most popular model, it is also the largest and most expensive, called Full.

It is manufactured in 2 materials, in white Melamine and in Multilaminate veneered and polished, both 18 mm thick. The marginal contribution coefficient is 40%.

The cost of materials is $57, including packaging for delivery, and the retail price is $95. The maintenance required is the addition of water as it evaporates from the containers naturally, approximately 1 glass or table glass every 3 or 4 days. No special training is required to use it, it is very intuitive, but despite this, we provide a user manual that explains the basics and some very simple tips.

pads.title: Regional transportation and energy systems for the Amazon
pads.snippet: The cost for replicating the regional transportation and energy systems proposed by Kara Solar is $250,000.

pads.title: Solid rain, retaining water for crops
pads.snippet:
Solid Rain (Lluvia Sólida) is a potassium-based, degradable, non-soluble, and non-toxic granular powder that, upon contact with water, expands and is capable of adsorbing up to 400 times its weight in water, *depending on the type of soil, water quality, climate, plant, etc. It is placed at the root and keeps it hydrated without irrigation or rain. It can be used for plants, crops, trees, gardens, pots, hydroponics, vegetables, etc. The plants will take in moisture according to their needs, ensuring stable and healthy growth, reducing irrigation frequencies, and taking advantage of and optimizing rainwater.

With water availability becoming increasingly difficult, Solid Rain aims to reduce water extraction for agriculture. It allows irrigation or rainwater to be used and made more efficient. It also reduces the risk of loss due to lack of water by reducing the frequency of irrigation by up to 90%.

Innovator: Leonardo Rico Fernández

pads.title: ABC Do Empreendedor
pads.snippet:
It provides tools that will help and guide entrepreneurs on the best way to start their business, considering all the important factors, whether financial, legal or management.

The portal is aimed at all types of entrepreneurs: new, newly started or already established, and provides a range of services in the same space: Business Plan, Feasibility Studies, Company Constitution, Model Documents, Virtual Accounting, Business Plans Marketing, Credit/Financing.

In addition to the above services, it supports entrepreneurs to find co-working spaces and multicredit.

pads.title: BusCenter
pads.snippet:
Based on functional and non-functional buses, with the aim of providing integrated infrastructure for the provision of services in the fields of STEAM Education, Health, Environment, Tourism, Entrepreneurship, culture and safe spaces for youth.

The project is already in 2 provinces: Luanda and Namibe, with itinerant and fixed buses that aim to promote STEM Education, Proximity Health, taking a Disease Screening and Diagnosis Center to communities, promoting culture, robotics and initiation space education, promoting free internet access and satellite telephony, as well as supporting local primary schools with digital literacy and a small library to encourage reading.

The project is in the expansion phase for the Entrepreneur's BusCenter, which aims to have a One-Stop-Center for the entrepreneur, that is, in the same space an entrepreneur who wants to open his business will be able to find all the services, from the feasibility study, company registration, brand registration, access to credit services, among others.

pads.title: Roque online
pads.snippet:
Their focus is to help anyone compete effectively in modern society. Whether you’re an informal market vendor, small business owner, or a large distributor, you can download the mobile application and start registering your inventory so we can start monetizing it on our website or through our partners’ ecommerce channels.

It's a team of individuals dedicated to connecting the informal markets of the world with empowering technologies. Inspirate is the famous Roque Santeiro open-air market in the Republic of Angola that operated from 1991 to 2011. This market was the largest of its kind in Africa and provided a valuable service during a period of significant strife in the country's history. These types of markets exist all over the world and we want consumers to connect with vendors and service providers with which they ordinarily wouldn't connect.

pads.title: AgriTPG
pads.snippet: Providing plantation statistics using satellite and drone imagery. They are launched in 2019 with a group of young Angolans. Their solution tries to close the knowledge gap. Challenges that they are facing during implementation were: Understanding the market and user needs, Procurement of technology vendors, Data collection issues.

pads.title: Mavo Diami (My Land) in Angola
pads.snippet:
The envisaged impact of the effective use of Mavo Diami services is strengthened the resilience of smallholder farmers to climate change; improved soil sustainability and land allocation; and improved self-reliance of smallholder farmers due to sustainable food production and improved income security. In turn, this will contribute to a more stable agricultural economy in Angola.

Mavo Diami from consortium led by Worldvision Netherlands. The Mavo Diami project funded under the Geo Data 4Agriculture and Water of the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Netherlands Space Agency. The aim of this project is to improve the food and income security of more than 100,000 smallholder farmers by accelerating their agri-business performance through informed decisions supported by the Mavo Diami services built on weather, water, soil, and crop signals and other relevant data and indicators. The project is called Mavo Diami, which means 'my land' in Angolan local language (Kimbundo). During the project the Kres network was formed as a social enterprise to carry on beyond the project.

pads.title: Digital Grow
pads.snippet: It has 1,500 active users and 2,300 registered users and deals with digital advisory through AgriVAS: One to many advisory covering agricultural livestock information and addressing knowledge gaps leading to low productivity. A resource centre - digital library, free access with technical documentation to support family farming, including books, technical articles, videos or practical exercises, being found in 4 languages: Portuguese, Spanish, French and English. The contents of the Digital Library are tailor-made, essentially for the most disadvantaged regions and a virtual Platform that, in partnership with universities and research centres in Africa and Latin America, promotes training at different levels, promoting transfer of know-how and South-South relations. Digital Grow develops technical training tailored and adjusted to the local reality, especially suitable for geographies with weak internet and less sophisticated devices, operating offline. The contents of this training allow the farmer a deeper knowledge of the entire production process and value chain, a better use of resources, a reduction in production costs and an increase in production and income. They use smartphones, a website and dashboard and portal, both local and cloud-based software. Their challenges are understanding the market, and user needs, accessibility, digital literacy and use by marginalized groups. Their funding has come from impact investors and donors and is dependent on them.

pads.title: GeoFarmer
pads.snippet: Whilst GeoTerraImage is a private sector company which provides actionable intelligence through monthly crop monitoring through GeoFarmer-©-Crop monitoring platform to support precision farming, and accurate information to map crop trends and statistics by using a dashboard in a cloud-based environment. The innovative solution provides through the use of computers, satellites and Earth Observation visual maps and illustrations, statistics and trends for each field or farm being analysed (crop type, crop growth stages, land suitability, crop irrigation) and guiding decision making around farm management and practices for more efficient and sustainable production. GeoTerraImage have reached wide scale sustained adoption and operate in Angola, Botswana, Comoros, DRC, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Through specialized software, proprietary algorithms and application GeoTerraImage use remote sensed data to create spatial information. They combine advanced information and reporting to enable analysis, quantification and monitoring to support key decision making. They charge business subscription fees for their fully commercial product and believe their technology is inclusive of underrepresented groups.

pads.title: Kobocollect
pads.snippet:
It addresses challenges such as difficulties in field information transmission, potential data loss on paper, decision-making hurdles due to insufficient knowledge of field realities, and complexities in updating forms for basic information collection.

Key Advantages:

-Time Efficiency: Eliminates the need to transcribe information from paper to mobile devices for analysis.

-Accuracy: Minimizes errors through validation post-entry, eliminating transcription errors.

-User-Friendly: Requires no technical expertise and can be quickly learned.

-Multimedia Options: Allows display, recording of images, videos, or GPS coordinates.

-Multilingual Support.

-Efficient Support for Monitoring Processes.

-Quick Data Analysis: The server organizes and consolidates information for rapid analysis.

-Continuous Updates.

-Controlled Access: Limits and scopes access to information.

-Cost-Effective.

Targeting humanitarian and development cooperation services, companies, and civil society organizations, KoboToolbox proves to be a valuable, efficient tool for data management and analysis in the field.

pads.snippet: Weather Impact provides agrometeorological forecast and advisory services to support smallholder farmer's decision-making.

pads.title: Agroportal
pads.snippet: This is a digital platform made up of complementary components (website, social networks and newsletters) and which serves as a vehicle for boosting Agribusiness in Angola, providing its users with several totally free services of great use and added value, as well as being a way to develop and promote business or a brand in this segment quickly and efficiently.

pads.title: KRES
pads.snippet: Launched in 2021, the KRES Network, operational in Angola and Mozambique, is a collaborative initiative involving partners from the Netherlands and World Vision. Serving as a decentralized service provider, it has 250 smartphone users and 2,800 basic phone users.

pads.title: Jardins da Yoba
pads.snippet: Jardins da Yoba integrate agricultural and livestock systems prioritize environmental sustainability and responsible resource utilization. Their core activities involve the production and multiplication of seeds, alongside cultivating vegetables and fruit trees. Additionally, they focus on honey and bee product production, as well as the organic crafting of sweets and jams. These endeavors represent their current and future potential for export, underscoring their commitment to excellence.

pads.title: Aldeia VILLAGE CAMELA AMÕES
pads.snippet: Aldeia Camela Amões, nestled amidst the Lumbanganda mountain range, spans 40,000 hectares, offering a multifaceted solution to combat poverty in vulnerable contexts.

pads.title: AfriYAN – Nayuca
pads.snippet:
This approach addresses a growing demand for sustainable and socially responsible products, offering long-term economic benefits and positive community impact. The project contributes to environmental sustainability by reducing waste through the adoption of reusable pads, which replaces disposable products and minimizes solid waste in landfills. 

Moreover, the use of reusable products results in lower resource consumption compared to disposable pads, which require significant amounts of trees, water, and energy for production. The social impact of the initiative is significant, particularly for low-income communities. The affordability of reusable pads and soap manufacturing creates accessible solutions, alleviating menstrual poverty and fostering income generation opportunities. By empowering women with greater control over their menstrual health, education, and work opportunities, the initiative strives to bring about positive change in communities.

pads.title: Tele-Educativo
pads.snippet:
The platform delivers Tele-guidance, Tele-education, and preventive diagnoses with the aim of averting:

Maternal mortality

Infant mortality

Early and unwanted pregnancies

Arterial hypertension

Thrombosis

Cardiovascular diseases

To facilitate this, the platform offers hospital-grade equipment that enables users to remotely monitor their parameters in the comfort of their homes. Their target audience includes girls aged 13 to 18 and working women aged 18 to 55.

pads.title: Kassai
pads.snippet:
Self paced platform, where healthcare professionals can take courses in their own time. All contents are approved by the Angolan Ministry of Health.

This platform is a partnership between the Ministry of Health of Angola and USAID – United Nations Agency International Development.

pads.title: Monani
pads.snippet:
This platform works as a pre- and post-natal counseling center. Every pregnant woman can register for free and receive every week, according to her gestation period, suggestions, and tips on a healthy and risk-free pregnancy.

How to join?

Just send a message to the number 46558 with the text monami, full name and gestation week number. Example: monami Antónia Jacinta 24

pads.title: Appy Saúde
pads.snippet:
It features details such as photos, addresses, directions, contacts, opening hours, services, associated insurance, and user feedback. The app covers health services nationwide, offering filtering options by zone, distance, and more.

Additionally, Appy Saúde facilitates the ordering, purchase, and delivery of over 18,000 pharmaceutical products from major pharmacies in Angola, offering price information and product descriptions. The app is available for free on the AppStore and Google Play Store, making it accessible for users seeking comprehensive healthcare information and convenient pharmaceutical services.

pads.title: OiMeninas App
pads.snippet: Through an interactive quiz format, the app addresses four key themes related to sexual and reproductive health and rights: Knowing your body, relationships, Sexuality, and Sexually transmitted diseases. Tailored questions, approved by the Ministry of Health, are categorized for different age groups. Users input their name and age to access questions appropriate to their age group. The responses contribute to generating statistical insights into users' knowledge levels, providing a foundation for the Ministry of Youth and Sports, Ministry of Health, and Ministry of Education to tackle challenges and enhance access to adolescent-friendly Sexual and Reproductive Health services. The app aims to empower adolescent girls and youth by fostering informed decision-making.

pads.title: Safe Deliver App
pads.snippet:
The App leverages the growing accessibility of mobile phones to provide life-saving information and guidance through easy-to-understand animated instruction videos, action cards, and drug lists. It can serve as a training tool both in pre-and in-service training and equips birth attendants even in the most remote areas with a powerful on-the-job reference tool. 

The App consists of 13 modules, with each module containing five features: videos, practical procedures, action cards, a drug list, and a self-examination platform called MyLearning.

The clinical content in the global app versions is based on global WHO guidelines rather than the directives of a specific country. In Angola, the content was also validated by the Ministry of Health.

This App aims to reinforce the efforts to reduce the maternal mortality ratio (239 deaths per 100,000 live births). The high fertility and maternal mortality in Angola are linked to low family planning coverage (14 percent) and to the fact that 50 percent of births are performed without a skilled attendant.

pads.title: SMSJOVEM/Ureport
pads.snippet:
The system comprises three modules:

1- SMS or WhatsApp requests: Users can send questions via SMS to U-Reporters, who respond with menu-based or personal messages.

2- Real-time polling/monitoring: This module gauges youth opinions on issues related to demand, access, prevention, care interventions, and behavioral changes.

3 - Campaigns: Mobilizing young people for positive community contributions, this module gathers valuable information to enhance their lives.

U-Report's primary goal is to address social norms and enhance understanding of knowledge, attitudes, and practices among youth. It plays a crucial role in promoting positive social and behavioral change, well-being, and health-seeking behaviors. Counselors provide anonymous support on various themes, including HIV prevention, family planning, early pregnancy, menstrual health, mental health, COVID-19, and employment.

In Angola, SMS Jovem/U-Report boasts over 95,000 enrolled adolescents and young people. Any Angolan with a cellphone can join the service by simply sending a message to 140, and it's free for UNITEL users.

pads.title: Machine à tisser solaire
pads.snippet: La machine à tisser solaire permet de tisser automatiquement les pagnes traditionnels burkinabé appélé Faso Danfani. Il permet d'alléger le travail manuel qu'effectuaient la plupart des femmes avec les mains et les pieds. En outre la machine utilise l'énergie solaire pour son fonctionnement donc pratique dans tous les milieux (urbain et rural). C'est donc une solution efficace, rapide, facile, économique et écologique.

pads.title: Cross-Border Collaboration Programme
pads.snippet:
1. Increased trust and cooperation: Cross-border collaboration programs can help build trust and cooperation among communities on both sides of the border. When people from different communities work together on common projects, they learn to understand and respect each other's perspectives, which can help reduce tensions and conflicts.
2. Improved economic opportunities: Cross-border collaboration programs can help create new economic opportunities for communities in border areas. By working together, communities can leverage their shared resources and strengths to develop new businesses and markets, which can lead to increased economic growth and stability.
3. Enhanced cultural exchange: Cross-border collaboration programs can facilitate cultural exchange and mutual learning between different communities. This can help promote greater appreciation and understanding of each other's cultural traditions and values, which can in turn foster greater social cohesion and harmony.
4. Enhanced conflict resolution mechanisms: Cross-border collaboration programs can help to develop and strengthen conflict resolution mechanisms, such as cross-border mediation and negotiation. This can help to prevent or resolve conflicts, which can contribute to increased social cohesion.

The Lake Turkana Cultural Festival, held annually on the border between Kenya and Ethiopia, celebrates the cultural diversity of the region and promotes peaceful coexistence between neighboring communities.

pads.title: Cross-Border Trade Associations to facilitate Trade and Cooperation across borders
pads.snippet:
1. Building relationships: EAGC helped to build relationships between grain traders, farmers, and other stakeholders in border areas. This has helped to promote trust and cooperation between people from different ethnic and national backgrounds. 

2. Providing a forum for dialogue: EAGC provided a forum for dialogue between different stakeholders in the grain sector. This has helped to promote understanding and cooperation between different groups. 

3. Improving livelihoods: By promoting trade and improving food security, EAGC helped to improve the livelihoods of people in border areas. This has helped to reduce tensions and promote social cohesion. 

4. Supporting cross-border trade: EAGC supported cross-border trade by providing information on market prices, quality standards, and other relevant issues. This has helped to promote economic integration and reduce barriers to trade. 

5. Supporting peace-building initiatives: EAGC supported peace-building initiatives in border areas by working with local communities and organizations. For example, EAGC has supported the establishment of grain trading centers in border areas, which has helped to promote economic development and reduce tensions.

pads.title: Sustainable Conflict Management Solution
pads.snippet:
1. Improved cross-border trade: RASMI facilitated the development of cross-border trade in the region, leading to increased economic opportunities for the people living in border areas. This has contributed to a reduction in tensions and conflicts related to competition for resources.


2. Increased community participation in conflict management: The project encouraged community members to participate in conflict management processes, fostering a sense of ownership and responsibility for peaceful coexistence. This has contributed to the strengthening of social cohesion in the region.


3. Enhanced intercultural understanding: The project provided opportunities for people from different cultures and backgrounds to interact and learn from one another. This helped to break down stereotypes and prejudices, leading to increased trust and respect between communities.


4. Strengthened institutional capacity: RASMI provided training and capacity building for local institutions and organizations involved in conflict management. This enhanced their ability to respond to conflicts in a timely and effective manner, contributing to the maintenance of social cohesion in the region.


5. Increased access to justice: The project supported the establishment of community justice mechanisms, providing an alternative to formal justice systems that may be inaccessible or inappropriate for some communities. This contributed to a sense of fairness and justice in the region.

pads.title: Community Based Development Tourism
pads.snippet:
1. Improved cross-border relations: The establishment of the park has improved relations between the governments of Botswana and South Africa, who jointly manage the park. This has had a positive impact on social cohesion in the border areas of the two countries, as it has led to increased cooperation and communication between communities on either side of the border.
2. Increased tourism: The Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park has become a popular destination for tourists, both from within southern Africa and from overseas. This has created economic opportunities for local communities, as businesses such as lodges, restaurants, and tour operators have sprung up to cater to the growing number of visitors.
3. Job creation: The establishment of the park has also created jobs for people living in the border areas, both in the tourism industry and in conservation efforts. This has had a positive impact on social cohesion, as it has provided opportunities for people from different communities to work together towards a common goal.
4. Conservation efforts: The park's conservation efforts have helped to protect animals and their habitats, which has had a positive impact on the natural environment in the border areas. This has also helped to promote social cohesion, as people from different communities have come together to support conservation efforts.

pads.snippet: Using satellite data to monitor forests carbone sequestration in order to raise carbon credits for the community and local reforestation projects

pads.title: ColesHill Traditional Slag Stove is a climate smart product that is focused on a reduction of cuin…
pads.snippet: ColesHill Traditional Slag Stove is a climate smart product that is focused on a reduction of cuing down of trees (deforestation) by using Copper Slag (a by-product of copper extraction by smelting) as the heat source, thereby contributing to climate action and an action to land pollution caused by industrial wastes. The innovator is a beneficiary of the Experimentation program with support of USD10,000 for material procurement, techncial support from the Copperbelt Univiersity and training in business development. More on the innovation on the following Sites: https://youtu.be/Ed2YD8o1QSM; https://web.facebook.com/search/top?q=coleshill%20zambia

pads.title: Agricultiural farming.
pads.snippet: e-Njavwa Innovation: Using a digital platform and real time data from the meteorological department , the system uses artificial Intelligence models and data analytics to determine the right crops to grow at a specific time. Propreitor, Anne Mwansa is part of the Experimentation program beneficiaries of USD10,000 support of material, NISIR technical support and business development mentorship.

pads.title: Solar Energy Financing Solutions
pads.snippet:
1. Renewable Energy Access: M-Kopa's solar energy systems provide households with access to renewable energy, reducing reliance on fossil fuels and decreasing greenhouse gas emissions.
2. Reduced Deforestation: By providing households with an alternative to wood and charcoal for cooking and lighting, M-Kopa's solar energy systems may contribute to reducing deforestation rates in the region.
3. Improved Health: By reducing exposure to indoor air pollution from traditional cooking methods, M-Kopa's solar energy systems may improve health outcomes for households in the region.
4. Economic Benefits: M-Kopa's pay-as-you-go model enables low-income households to access energy services that they might otherwise not be able to afford, potentially increasing economic resilience in the face of climate change impacts.
5. Community Building: M-Kopa has also partnered with organizations such as the Red Cross to distribute solar energy systems in refugee camps, providing energy access to vulnerable populations and potentially building community resilience to climate-related shocks.

pads.title: Climate Resilient in Post Harvest and Value chain Solutions
pads.snippet:
1. The CSAYN Hub Rwanda has trained over 600 young farmers on climate-smart agriculture practices, resulting in the adoption of these practices on over 1,000 hectares of farmland.
2. Through partnerships with microfinance institutions, the organization has provided access to financing to over 150 farmers, enabling them to invest in their farms and adopt sustainable agriculture practices.
3. The adoption of sustainable agriculture practices has resulted in a 30% increase in maize yields and a 50% increase in bean yields in some areas where the CSAYN Hub Rwanda operates.
 4. The organization has helped to establish 13 seed banks in border areas of Rwanda, which have distributed over 1,500 kilograms of improved seed varieties to farmers, resulting in increased crop yields.

pads.title: Agro-business Solutions.
pads.snippet:
1. In 2020, Komaza planted over 1 million trees in Kenya, resulting in the sequestration of approximately 112,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide.
2. Komaza has provided over 27,000 farmers with training and support on sustainable forestry practices, resulting in the establishment of over 30,000 hectares of tree farms.
3. Komaza's microfinance program has disbursed over $3 million in loans to farmers since its inception, resulting in the establishment of over 9,000 hectares of tree farms and the creation of over 7,000 jobs.
 4. A 2019 study conducted by the World Agroforestry Centre found that the agroforestry model used by Komaza resulted in a 34% increase in maize yields and a 21% increase in income for farmers in the areas where it operates.

pads.title: Energy Access in Off-Grid areas.
pads.snippet:
Agri-equipment Financing using Innovative Pay plans:


1. Increased access to irrigation: In many parts of Kenya and Uganda, farmers rely on rainfall to water their crops. However, with unpredictable weather patterns and droughts becoming more frequent, irrigation is becoming increasingly important. 3. Reduced energy costs: Solar power has enabled farmers to reduce their reliance on fossil fuels, which can be expensive and environmentally damaging. By using solar-powered equipment, farmers can save money on energy costs, which can be reinvested into their farms. For example, in Kenya, the Solar Energy for Agriculture and Livelihoods project has enabled farmers to save up to 50% on their energy costs.

pads.snippet:

In response to this need, an innovative system has been developed that uses sensor technology, WiFi connectivity and cloud services to assess and visualize water quality and provide timely alerts to users.

This is a program for a water quality detector using a home sensor. The program measures water conductivity, calculates the TDS (Total Dissolved Solids) value, and sends the data to ThingSpeak for real-time viewing and monitoring. In addition, it uses the Twilio service to send text messages with the water quality classification according to the ranges established by the World Health Organization (WHO). It also includes functionality to sense water temperature using a DS18B20 sensor.

pads.title: How weaving empowers women deprived of their liberty
pads.snippet:
In 2018, it was detected that only 16/32 entities in Mexico registered some post-penitentiary program for women, such as agreements to form a job bank or with companies so that they employ the graduated population. In addition, only 13 have a periodic advice or assistance program for the graduated population.

LA CANA is a social project that seeks to create job opportunities for women in prison, through the implementation of programs and workshops aimed at their personal development, as well as work and job training, in order to promote a reintegration process that contributes to reducing recidivism and crime rates in the country.

La Cana trains women deprived of their liberty in various weaving, embroidery, sewing, macramé and textile weaving techniques through a weekly workshop held in each of the prisons where we work. The purpose of this is to help them learn a trade in which they can be remunerated away from delinquency. Subsequently, they are in charge of selling the handmade products made by the women in prison, to whom they deliver the proceeds from the sale of their work. In addition to the above, they carry out other productive work for the development and learning of skills and abilities, as well as mental health workshops for the personal growth of the inmates.

"While listening to the stories of women inmantes, we detected that in many of them the common factor was the structural gender violence to which they have been subjected, which greatly influenced how they ended up in prison,” explains Wendy Balcázar, of La Cana, who has a degree in Law.

Through special projects and orders, they also connect fashion and product designers with women deprived of liberty, supporting an alternative labor market.

(Source: https://www.lacana.mx/pages/quienes-somos )

pads.title: Theater, visual materials and collective solutions to stop damaging extractive projects
pads.snippet:
Back in 2013, the Mexican government passed the Reforma Energética, which, amongst other things, allows the use of hydraulic fracturing, also known as fracking, as a gas extraction and exploitation method (Alternativas y Capacidades, 2018). The Huasteca Potosina has abundant natural resources, and, because of this, it became Petróleos Mexicanos (PEMEX)’s target for fracking. 

One of the main actors involved in the movement against fracking in the Huasteca region is the Coordinadora de Organizaciones Campesinas e Indígenas de la Huasteca Potosina (COCIHP; Coordinator of Farmer and Indigenous Organizations of the Huasteca Potosina). COCIHP is a civil association formed in July 1994. Its members are 12 grassroots organizations at the municipal level (in 6 municipalities) of indigenous Nahuatl, Teenek, campesino, and women producers in the coffee, citrus, and pile farming sectors (Wiser). COCIHP’s main objective is to prevent and prohibit fracking in the municipality of Xilitla, through the respect of Ejido and Community Regulations by the municipal authority. According to Alternativas y Capacidades AC (2018), they have a methodology for the Community Training Process:

They bring together the committees, neighborhood leaders and neighbors of the community in plenary sessions at the invitation of the ejido and community authorities.

They inform through analogies the framework of indigenous peoples' rights, especially the right to regulate community life.

They perform small theater plays to represent the actions of the companies to implement fracking in the territory.

Provide visual support materials appropriate to the context and audiences: videos, maps, printouts of the regulatory law.

Brainstorming for the community to collectively identify and visualize community issues.

Collectively identify solutions to the problems including the slogan NO TO FRACKING in the community.

They draft the Community Regulations and present them to the community and the Community Assembly votes on their approval.

Following these guidelines, and mainly dialoguing with the authorities and mobilizing the communities, the COCIHP has succeeded in getting the City Council to declare itself Fracking Free.

According to the same Alternativas y Capacidades document, some of the challenges that COCIHP found were 1) trust with people and community authorities, 2) remoteness of the communities, and 3) people who speak an indigenous language. They faced these challenges by 1) strategic networking with people close to the community authorities in order to have a direct link and build trust with the communities; 2) COCIHP has partnered with other CSOs that have budgets for training activities. Given the scarcity of public transportation, COCIHP made alliances with local people so that they could transport them to the communities; and 3) COCIHP is accompanied by translators of the Náhuatl and Téenek languages to facilitate communication. It also translates the word "fracking" into the two languages to provide clarity on the impact of fracking.

Petra, seen from a different angle! You will undoubtedly enjoy a tour that you won’t forget thanks to your local guide - Ma'moun Al-Nawafleh - who was born and raised in Wadi Musa. He will contribute his enthusiasm for Petra, the same enthusiasm that was passed down from his father.

The trip begins at Petra Visitor Center, where you will meet Ma'moun and start your tour. Here, you will learn about the renowned Nabatean civilisation, archeoastronomy of Petra, and the old clocks that are carved into its ancient walls.

After enjoying a delicious traditional supper and watching the sunset from Al-Bayda area, you may begin your stargazing experience with a laser pointer and telescope to explore the night mesmerizing sky.

pads.title: Rum Sky
pads.snippet:
The experience begins with a 20-minute presentation, taking you on a journey that illuminates the foundation of our solar system and allows you to travel to all parts of the universe.

As the presentation concludes, the stargazing experience begins across the starlit sky with high-quality telescopes and a brief explanation of reading the stars and navigating.

You will have a night full of stars!

pads.title: Cycling Jordan
pads.snippet:
Embark on an exciting biking adventure in Jordan with Cycling Jordan! Choose from a selection of pre-arranged cycling activities or let them create a tour exclusively for you. Personalize your experience by selecting the sights you want to see, the duration of your bike ride, and your fitness level, while the Cycling Jordan team takes care of the rest! Join a group of fellow bikers on an organized excursion and maximize your approximately one-week vacation in Jordan. Discover the country's stunning scenery on two wheels as you ride through some of the most scenic sections of the Jordan bike trail, witness breathtaking vistas, and engage with local communities.

Each tour provides a one-of-a-kind cycling or mountain biking experience. Cycling Jordan offers a diverse range of single-day tours to various destinations, offering unique experiences and unexpected attractions for bikers of all fitness levels. Whether you're searching for an extreme adventure or a family-friendly day trip, Cycling Jordan has something for everyone!

pads.title: Hiking & Camping at Umm Qais
pads.snippet:
Hiking at Umm Qais allows your soul to reconnect with nature while allowing your mind to experience learning about the culture and history of a place once unknown to you.

With Ahmad Al-Omari, a local guide who was born and raised in Umm Qais, you will go on a hike to learn about the area's history, culture, environment, flora diversity, and beautiful landscapes.

A camping experience is also available and is ideal for adventurous travelers, as you will help set up the camps, prepare the food, and expand the campfire.

You will have a one-of-a-kind night filled with breathtaking scenes as you look out over the spectacular Tabariah lake and Golan heights!

pads.title: Frog Man Diving
pads.snippet:
Diving with Hashem Shmayleh in Aqaba is not just a thrilling adventure but also an educational experience that focuses on understanding and appreciating the local culture and marine life. Shmayleh's expertise as a certified diving instructor ensures that visitors are well-prepared and safe throughout the dive trip, while his passion for sharing knowledge about the area's traditions and sea life enriches the overall experience. With stunning marine life and shipwrecks to explore, diving with Shmayleh is an unforgettable adventure for all skill levels.

In addition to providing a thrilling diving experience, Hashem Shmayleh also focuses on sustainable tourism practices and responsible diving. He emphasizes the importance of respecting the marine environment and minimizing the impact of diving on the delicate ecosystems of the Red Sea.

As part of his commitment to responsible tourism, Shmayleh also participates in regular beach cleanups and encourages his clients to do the same. He believes that by educating visitors about the importance of conservation and sustainable tourism practices, we can help to preserve the natural beauty of Aqaba's Red Sea for future generations to enjoy.

pads.title: Levant Vista Resort
pads.snippet:
Located amidst the picturesque landscapes of Ajloun, the Levant Vista Resort beckons travellers seeking a sustainable yet comfortable retreat. This enchanting haven seamlessly blends into its natural surroundings, providing guests with a serene and eco-friendly accommodation experience.

The resort boasts a collection of charming wooden cabins, thoughtfully designed with sustainability in mind. Inside, guests will find modern amenities that ensure a comfortable stay, while still maintaining a strong commitment to eco-conscious practices.

Nature enthusiasts will delight in the resort's proximity to pristine hiking trails, winding through the captivating forests and hills of Ajloun. Embarking on these trails, visitors can immerse themselves in the beauty of the natural landscape, breathe in the crisp mountain air, and encounter rich biodiversity that thrives in this region.

For those seeking a delightful outdoor culinary experience, the resort provides ready-equipped areas for BBQs and picnics. The designated areas are designed to blend seamlessly into the environment, ensuring that the experience remains sustainable and respectful of the surroundings.

pads.title: Mount Burqesh Eco Camp
pads.snippet:
Welcome to the enchanting Mount Burqesh eco-tourism camp nestled amidst the breathtaking green hills of Ajloun. This sustainable haven is a sanctuary for nature enthusiasts and those seeking an authentic cultural experience.

The accommodation facilities, designed with sustainability in mind, seamlessly merge with the natural surroundings, allowing visitors to reconnect with nature without compromising on comfort.

One of the highlights of Mount Burqesh is undoubtedly the mesmerising view of Ajloun’s verdant hills that unfold before the guests’ eyes. The culinary experience here is a delightful journey into the rich flavours of Jordanian cuisine. Traditional dishes, prepared with locally sourced ingredients, satisfy taste buds and transport guests to a realm of culinary indulgence.

To complement the journey, the camp offers traditionally flavoured tea infused with a medley of aromatic herbs, carefully selected from the surrounding hills. This invigorating beverage invigorates the senses and provides a refreshing respite during leisurely walks through the camp's lush surroundings.

pads.title: Beit Al-Reef
pads.snippet: Beit Al-Reef Jerash Eco Camp beckons you to discover its hidden charm, where nature, culture, and community intertwine to create a truly memorable journey. Immerse yourself in lush forests, hike scenic trails, and enjoy captivating performances by the "Al-Waradat" folkloric band. Delight in authentic Jordanian cuisine and get ready to embrace the extraordinary where every moment is filled with wonder and adventure. Experience the harmony of nature, culture, and community at the camp.

pads.title: Khallet Al Saadeh Camp
pads.snippet:
Khallet Al-Saadeh, a remarkable sustainable eco-tourism camp nestled in the heart of Ajloun, where nature and culture intertwine to create an unforgettable experience. This eco-friendly haven not only offers comfortable accommodation facilities but also showcases lands of olive tree farms.

Immersed in the tranquility of the surrounding landscape, guests can unwind in eco-friendly accommodations that seamlessly blend with the natural environment. By choosing to stay here, visitors contribute to the preservation of Ajloun's pristine beauty. Adding to the allure of the camp, guests have the unique opportunity to explore the bountiful lands of fruits. Throughout the seasons, visitors can engage in the joyful act of fruit picking, selecting ripe and juicy treasures from a variety of orchards. The experience is not only fulfilling but also offers a deeper connection to the land and its abundant offerings.

Beyond the breathtaking views, the camp provides a culinary adventure that celebrates Jordanian traditions. Delightful aromas waft through the air as guests indulge in a feast of traditional delicacies prepared with locally sourced ingredients.

pads.title: Seed Bombs Making -Beit Al Ward
pads.snippet:
Beit Al Ward - translates to 'House of Flowers'. Your journey will begin in Beit Al Ward, where a couple had decided to transform their own garden into a beautiful greenhouse with over 400 different types of plants.

Spend an hour with Wijdan - your host, and the owner of Beit Al Ward - where you will be welcomed and briefed about this wonderful initiative. This will be followed by a tour of the lovely home garden and an informative activity on how to make seed bombs.

You may take the seed bomb up on a hiking/biking trip and leave it in the soil of nature to grow once it has rained, or take it back home and plant it!

pads.title: Yousef Honey - Beekeeping
pads.snippet:
Different flowers grow and boom in different seasons and based on that, there are three honey flavors in the three honey harvests of a year.

Yousef, the beekeeper, will guide you through a beekeeping journey that will end in his workshop. There you will be able to extract honey from honeycombs. This experience is a complete demonstration of the honey production process.

pads.title: Beesan Beekeeping
pads.snippet:
An experience that allows you to live as a beekeeper in the heart of Jerash, and learn honey production from a local family who has inherited the honey industry from their forefathers.

The family also offers traditional meals from breakfast and lunch. After breakfast in the backyard, a hiking trip is available to the apiary location. You will gear up with the special beekeeper suit and begin the bee experience there.

pads.title: Al-Safi Kitchen
pads.snippet:
Abduljawad Al-Asheibat, a resident of Ghour Al-Safi in Jordan 🇯🇴 creates a thriving tourist destination for his hometown with his unique eco-agro-gastro #travelexperience - one of the www.traveljordanian.com experiences that we support with funding from @nlinjo.

Through a holistic blend of soul-healing wellness activities including yoga and meditation🧘🏾‍♂ , immersive bedouin experience like jameed making, farmland exploration and seasonal crop gathering.🌿🌱🧺 and other experiences provided by the local community, such as canyoneering 🧗🏽‍♂️ hiking🥾and biking🚴🏽, Abdeljawad plans to showcase the area's rich archaeology and heritage to attract more visitors.

pads.title: Balloons Over Rum
pads.snippet:
Fayez AlKhlaifat recognises the importance of providing authentic and captivating experiences that leave his visitors with an indelible mark on Jordan's cultural and natural landscape.

His latest offering, "Balloons over Rum" takes #adventuretravellers on an epic balloon flight over the magnificent #WadiRum desert.🪂🏜️🐫 From the serene terrains and breathtaking rock formations to the towering mountains, visitors from around the world can enjoy Jordan high up in the skies! 🌤️

pads.title: Bayt Al-Mahbash
pads.snippet:
👋🏽Meet Samer Al-Freihat from Ajloun 🇯🇴, who preserves culture and tradition through his family-owned venture - "Bayt Al-Mahbash". From crafting traditional Mahabash and wooden staff to other custom pieces, his passion gleams through his work.✨

With our technical and financial support to Samer through the CERA project, he is able to invest in machinery that would help him boost production and workplace safety. 🛠️🦺 In Jordan, we support 90 other #MSMEs with potential to access and compete in local and international #supplychains

Looking ahead, Samer dreams of participating in international bazaars, showcasing his traditional treasures to American and European markets.

pads.title: Beit Sweimeh Restaurant
pads.snippet:
In the heart of the Jordan Valley 🇯🇴 lies Beit Sweimeh restaurant, an eco-agro-gastro experience that blends tradition and cuisine. 🌱🍴 Run with love by Sireen Al Shareef, a mother of four, the restaurant radiates sustainability, community spirit and local charm.🌟

With the help of 15 talented local women crafting traditional foods, Beit Sweimeh is driving #femaleparticipation in the region's booming #tourism sector. They use organic methane gas, generated from leftover food to power the restaurant, while hydroponic farming nurtures organic crops grown on-site.👨🏽‍🌾🧺 A true eco-conscious haven!

pads.title: Ecological menstrual pads
pads.snippet:
MenstruAcción Querétaro is a collective which aims to raise awareness about menstrual education. They tour municipalities in the state of Queretaro, Mexico, where they educate about menstruation, distribute brochures with information, and carry out activities such as making ecological menstrual pads made out of cloth. (Source: https://www.facebook.com/menstruaccionqro/ ) 

The collective has also had an impact on public policy: On May 19, 2022, a reform to Law 7, section 30, of the Queretaro Women's Institute was approved, proposed by the MenstruAcción collective, in pursuit of dignified menstruation for Queretaro women, with the objective of taking into account dignified menstruation in existing laws. (Source: https://conecta.tec.mx/es/noticias/queretaro/educacion/aprobada-alumnas-tec-reforman-ley-favor-de-la-menstruacion-digna#:~:text=El%20pasado%2019%20de%20mayo,digna%20de%20las%20mujeres%20queretanas. )

pads.title: Menos plástico es fantástico
pads.snippet:
The type of microplastics known as nurdles, pellets, or siren's tears appear in the Caribbean paradise of Mahahual, in Quintana Roo. These are small fragments of plastic resin that are melted down to create larger products like bottles and pose a severe danger to marine wildlife and humans. A group of activists led by a woman trying to identify where the plastics came from and fight to raise awareness within her community, key actors and government.

pads.snippet:

pads.title: Eco Youth Group
pads.snippet: Eco Youth Jordan is the first environmental community group in Jordan led by women from Jordan and has recently grown to include females from Canada and China. It was established in the rural city of Ajloun where environmental awareness was close to non-existent. We aspired to change this statement across the country by creating a team, that consists of females who share a passion for protecting our fragile planet, and who strive to be the voice of women in the fields of agriculture and water.

pads.snippet: Our natural fertilisers will help refuse from all kinds of chemicals in cultivation of plants, because they are not only completely natural, but overpower chemical fertilisers in terms of efficiency. This innovative method, using the unique compost earthworms “Staratel”, indeed allows us to say that our vermicompost has the value of gold and is an irreplaceable organic fertiliser. Our production unit, situated in a quiet and green nook of Palestine, creates a miracle of nature, which already now is used by professional farmers and gardening enthusiasts in various countries across the world. Due to this we pay special attention to ensure that the range of our offer would include products for various climate zones and types of plants.

pads.title: Moringa for Sewage Water and Clean Energy
pads.snippet: Although water makes up to 71% of the Earth’s surface, only 0.5% is fresh. Fresh water resources are getting exhausted at an exponential rate due to environmental changes, as well as the lack of sustainable planning. This project addresses three of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs); Clean Water and Sanitation (SDG 6), Affordable and Clean Energy (SDG 7), and Zero Hunger (SDG 2). People living in small towns or villages with no access to central services, will be the main beneficiaries of this project. The project is about developing a decentralized sewage unit for sewage purification for agricultural uses; the products are methane gas that serves as a source of energy, and agriculture fertilizers and water. The sewage bulk is filtered through a net, aerated, mixed with grinded moringa seed, and finally charcoal to remove color, taste, and odor. Moringa Oleifera (MO) is widely cultivated in Egypt; its seeds contain 35–40% oil, with potent antimicrobial activity as well as effective coagulant and heavy metal removal properties. The COD, BOD, TDS, and other bacterial count tests are carried out to ensure the suitability of the produced water for agriculture. Therefore, MO can be considered a natural and cheap alternative for chlorine and aluminum sulfate. Through this project, the sewage water treatment unit could be cost-effective and eco-friendly by sustaining the fresh drinking water and increasing the availability of agricultural water and natural safe fertilizers. This eventually leads to increasing crops production and supports the country’s economy.

pads.title: Safe and Clean
pads.snippet: Safe & Clean is a dynamic waste management company with an unique approach to managing waste for a friendlier environment. We specialize in total waste management and recycling management services according to the so-called 5 R-principles, namely Rethink, Re-use, Reduce, Recycle and Remove and the Circular Economy.

eRecycleHUB - a digital recycling marketplace that provides users accessible tools to participate in recycling and sort at source. We are using technology and smart solutions in waste management & recycling service to enable users to identify the recyclability of certain waste items in just a CLICK

eRecycleHUB - a Social Impact Green Tech Enterprise that motivates people to earn profits out of their recyclables, live more sustainable & eco conscious lifestyle and be socially responsible.

pads.title: Al Numeira Environmental Association
pads.snippet:
Al Numeira Environmental Association is a local non-governmental Organization based in South Ghor community, Dead Sea, Jordan, founded on 2012 by a group of local people trying to make a difference and managing with their local resources, reporting the Jordanian environmental Ministry.

Our activities are focusing on sustainable development through two processes : raising the environmental awareness of the local community and engaging local human resources in sustainable tourism activities. 

Four main areas of work: grey water, permaculture, sustainable buildings, composting, and bicycle tourism

pads.title: Turkish Coffee Waste & Agar Agar
pads.snippet:
“I was trying the recipe of "Agar Agar+Clay" recipe by @fabtextiles & @fabricademy founder Anastasia Pistofidou, from her Bioplastic Cook Book when I noticed how similar the texture of the clay was to the wastes of Turkish coffee.

I decided to replicate the recipe using dried used Turkish coffee grounds. The first few results weren't what I hoped for, and there was several iterations before getting to this recipe.

The resulting material has a rubbery texture, it can be described as a soft solid that's a little flexible. I've tried soaking this resulting pieces in water for almost a week, and they kept their characteristics, so now I'm trying to develop and test the usage of this material as a coffee cup.

pads.title: The Duke's Diwan
pads.snippet:
The Duke's Diwan is one of the oldest, well-preserved stone buildings located in the heart of Amman. Built in 1924 by Abdul Rahman Madi, the building served as the Central Post Office, and after 1948, it hosted the Haifa Hotel.

In 2001 it caught the attention of Mamdouh Bisharat, the "Duke of Mukheibeh," who rented the house to protect it from destruction, with the aim of keeping the city's authenticity and character alive for Jordan's citizens and visitors.

Mamdouh converted the house on Faisal Str. into a Diwan, which traditionally means "council chamber," where people, thinkers, poets and artists meet. The Diwan's doors are always open for visitors, as well as for talents in all fields of culture.

pads.title: Project Sea
pads.snippet: A local scubadiving initiative that organizes monthly cleanup events in Aqaba (Red Sea)

pads.title: Youth for Climate Jordan
pads.snippet:
Youth for Climate Jordan is a climate youth movement that seeks to limit the consequences of the climate and biodiversity crisis by uniting as a movement and exerting political pressure while raising awareness in society.

For this, we believe that an immediate system change is absolutely necessary! Therefore, we protest, mobilize youth and organize ourselves as activists. As a movement, we believe that it is highly important to share the same values in order to reach these goals. To limit global warming properly and create a system change, we believe that a better world for everyone should be created, in which these values are incorporated.

pads.title: Petra Green Community Enterprise (PetraGCE)
pads.snippet:
Petra Green Community Enterprise "PetraGCE"​ was established after years of research and effort aimed at finding the ideal solutions to water issues in arid regions. Many aspects of water treatment were thoroughly researched by Jordanian professionals, including nanotechnologies in water treatment, development operations of household water treatment systems, and how to find efficient and sustainable alternatives to minimize the water waste. The pinnacle of these efforts was finding a method for completely eliminating water waste in household water treatment systems operating by reverse osmosis by %100.

PetraGCE works in the following sectors: Water, Energy and Food. Targeting local Jordanian and neighborhood markets through providing environmentally friendly solutions, products and services for the purpose of improving and upgrading their clients’ existing processes, products, services to be more environmentally friendly.

PetraGCE provides variety of solutions, products and service:

• Innovative solutions for water issues, which include:

o Reverse Osmosis systems – Zero waste – PETRA-RO180

o Reverse Osmosis systems – Zero waste – PETRA-RO75

o PetraGCE rationalization unit (patentable product) – PETRA-RU

o PetraGCE Grey Water systems (Rasheed system)

• Design systems which respond to the needs of customers in most efficient and effective ways.

Moreover; PetraGCE provide capacity building, consultations and technical assistance support to equip Jordanian youth with skills and knowledge through job preparation, training, and mentoring/coaching to empower them to obtain better and more sustainable jobs in their geographic locations.

pads.title: Greening the Camps
pads.snippet: Greening The Camps is a non-profit organisation that designs, develops, builds and maintains rooftop gardens in Palestinian refugee camps. The project is driven by our passion for environment and earthcare and our understanding of urban design and its toolsets. Sharing and gathering knowledge, as well as creating a truly sustainable livelihood are closely linked with our devotion to enrich impoverished urban and camp areas. The multi-layered process is, on every level, guided by the ideas and desires of the local community with whom we work. Through reconnecting displaced communities with food production from urban agricultural practices, we try to create opportunities for local empowerment and economic development.

pads.title: ARD Agriculture & Regenerative Development
pads.snippet:
ARD Agriculture & Regenerative Development is an agricultural company registered in Jordan dedicated to promote organic & regenerative agriculture and ecological restoration.

​

Founded in 2020 it aims to bridge and nurture the link between the world of agriculture and society for a positive ecological impact in Jordan and beyond.

​

ARD was born out of our deep concern about climate change and our ultimate goals are climate change mitigation, adaptation and impact reduction through the spread of regenerative agriculture - agricultural practices that remove carbon from the atmosphere and put it back in the soil - in Jordan and the region. 

​

ARD centre is located in Taybeh Organic Farms, Wadi Rajeb, Ajloun, Jordan.

pads.title: Midorization Project
pads.snippet:
A Japan-based social enterprise focusing on 1) Forest Regeneration & Biodiversity Restoration; 2) Saving Endangered Native Trees; 3) Awareness Raising & Knowledge Transfer; and 4) Research & Data Collection. Through the The Midorization Project, founder Motoharu NOCHI  introduced the first Miyawaki forest in the Arab world , and conducted forest regeneration as green infrastructure project with the Greater Amman Municipality, Jordanian Ministry of Environment, and GIZ. He is currently working on regenerating a Native Urban Forest in a public park in the heart of Amman in collaboration with a CBO Khidr Collective and Invest Bank. He has also been involved with starting up native sapling productions with local public and private nurseries. Nochi received his Bachelor’s degree in Interdisciplinary Studies from Global College, Long Island University, USA, in 2006, and received training in forest regeneration using the Miyawaki Method (India 2018; Lebanon 2019; Turkey 2019; Japan 2018, 2019, & 2022).

source: https://hayyjameel.org/whats-on/the-midorization-project/#:~:text=About%20The%20Midorization%20Project&text=Through%20the%20The%20Midorization%20Project,Ministry%20of%20Environment%2C%20and%20GIZ.

pads.title: Smart Green for Agritech Solutions
