Our Smart Systems help farmers to reach the optimum use of water and fertilizers by delivering the precise amount of water and nutrients to plants in a timely manner, thus saving up to 70% of water consumption, all by providing remote control of farms’ irrigation anytime, anywhere, and at a competitive price.

pads.title: Soft robotics using natural materials
pads.snippet:
Soft-robotics are based in Bio-inspired design or biomimicry and have applications in wearables, rehabilitation prosthetics, surgical robots, rescuing and others. I focused on the fabrication of soft actuators, sensors and grippers using novel materials, artificial muscles and performative locomotion design.

The Highlight of this week was experimenting on bio exploration drafting my own Bio silicone - embedding food waste from olives (usually thrown in the garbage at the end process of extracting Olive Oil) so instead of throwing this garbage here I am making soft-robotics out of them and ill explain below how I did it

pads.title: Biochromes
pads.snippet: Exploring colouring alternatives to the current ones. Bridging craftsmanship techniques and technology, to explore alternative colour sources and their processing. Ranging from plant based, insect base and bacteria based pigments.

pads.title: Circulamic
pads.snippet:
Circulamic by B.O.R is a clever way to add a partition between spaces that also helps with acoustics. The design is customizable and modular, adding both texture and color to a space while also helping to disguise what’s behind it.

I further developed this and used recycled material from the lab, I also included machines and digital fabrication tools like a heat press to better stick the joints I designed on Rhino + grasshopper and I found out that this structure/piece is useful in many applications as you see here in the pictures, this can be wearables like a skirt, top or part of the Shirts to add more design and coverage to certain clothes you already have at the same time this can be adjusted to wall curtain/partition. Optimizing the flexibility of both Applications as well as transparency options.

pads.title: BioFabricating Materials
pads.snippet: In this last century, we have been crafting, designing, and growing materials independently from their future use. This has caused major design flaws in our daily lives, where we find ourselves surrounded by plastics, while observing knowledge about local materials and techniques disappear and left unused even when in abundance. This research focused on exploring material alternatives to the current ones. By bridging craftsmanship techniques and today's easier access to technologies, exploring alternative material resources to craft their processing and develop products and materials hand in hand.

pads.title: Kombucha leather + Kombucha House Incubator
pads.snippet:
A DIY device that can be digitally fabricated in any laboratory and used from anybody in the world. It is equipped with a network of sensors, heating element and a fan to recreate the best conditions for growing bacteria cellulose in different locations. The incubator is connected to he network through a WIFI module and allows people to monitor in real time the fermenation process and the growth of the leather and share data.
As a naturally sustainable material, kombucha leather has many advantages. Unlike traditional leather, kombucha leather can be grown with zero waste, in tubs shaped as garment pattern pieces.

pads.snippet: Elbow that can be used to connect rain gutters or pipes.

pads.title: Raschel Mesh
pads.snippet: It is a type of knitted fabric that is used in a wide variety of applications, from clothing to the manufacture of industrial products. According to the literature consulted, it is the recommended mesh to collect water.

pads.title: Saran for shade
pads.snippet: Plastic material used in different areas for its resistance and price. It is usually used for shade but can be useful for collecting fog water.

pads.title: PVC Tile
pads.snippet: Plastic shingles fulfill the same harvesting function as sheets, but aesthetically they could be better. A disadvantage is that they could generate some type of water loss due to their structure.

pads.title: Plastic concrete tile
pads.snippet: plastic tiles produced with recycled plastic resin. It is shock resistant and has a lifespan of up to 100 years.

pads.title: Geomembrane
pads.snippet: they are geosynthetic sheets that ensure the sealing of a surface. They are typically used to remedy water losses by infiltration or to prevent the migration of contaminants into the soil.

pads.title: Polyethylene plastic tarpaulins
pads.snippet: this form could be a substitute for the use of solid structures such as sheets or coated roofs, so it means greater ease of installation and also that they can be temporary rain collectors.

pads.title: Aluzinc Sheets
pads.snippet: Aluzinc has a high resistance to corrosion and also protects against abrasion. It also has very good thermal and light reflection properties.

pads.title: PVC sheets
pads.snippet: it is a resistant and durable material. Most pipes and water reservoirs are made of this material.

pads.title: Women collective of electric taxis
pads.snippet:
The Guerreras Fénix of Umán, are a group of entrepreneurs, who started a women's taxi service to generate resources, without neglecting their children, families or their studies.

Within the group there are women between the ages of 18 and over 60, some divorced, retired, students, but all with the aim of doing good for their community. Their goal in a few years is to open work spaces for more women in other locations, and even entering the labor market in Mérida, “I wish the government would take into account all the sacrifices one makes; motorcycle taxis are not a regular job, and I am in it, I want the well-being of my workers. The last thing that I am doing, I am managing so that the ladies have the social security and the housing loans, like any company”.

They also continuosly create community initiatives to support health, children, and the environment. Their latest action is the electric transition of their motocabs to eliminate their pollution.

pads.title: Solar ice
pads.snippet: Solar Ice is an ice factory, whose main value offer is the commitment to the environment, focusing on the energy efficiency with which it operates its ice manufacturing plant.Located in the city of Chilpancingo, Solar Ice's manufacturing, storage and distribution plant is equipped with the latest in solar energy production technology, making it an energy self-sustaining factory.The water with which the ice is made is extracted from a spring, free of toxic agents, which is transported and treated under the highest quality standards in the industry.

pads.title: Conversion of machines from fuel to electric energy
pads.snippet:
MPS is a start-up in Monterrey, Mexico that assists anyone with an old car or a gas or diesel machinery to convert their energy source to electricity. In the case of any vehicle or machinery, they start by eliminating the components that will not be of use: the main engine, the gear, the cooling, and the exhaust system, the fuel tank, and everything related to fuel.

Then they adapt and take advantage of existing parts using the same manual transmission, brake system, and electrical system.

Finally, they install new components. The electric motor, its controller, and the battery are the vital elements of the system. Additionally, other auxiliary and control components are installed.

pads.title: Mini grids for safe and affordable water supply to rural households
pads.snippet:
In Bangladesh, approximately 73 million individuals still lack access to safe water within their own homes. Merely 2% of rural households have the privilege of obtaining water through a piped water supply, meaning that an overwhelming 98% of rural households in Bangladesh are deprived of this convenience. The arduous task of collecting water falls on women and girls, who spend up to two hours each day engaged in this chore. Moreover, majority of households rely on potentially hazardous tube wells. Consequently, rural families, particularly children, face a heightened risk of diarrhoea, malnutrition, and stunted growth.

As a solution to this pressing issue, Max TapWater develops and operates mini grids for the provision of piped water supply, aiming to bring easy, safe, and affordable water to rural households in Bangladesh. By availing

this water supply services, households gain access to a continuous 24/7 water supply directly from their taps, with a minimum allocation of 80-100 litres per person per day across three water points within their homes (kitchen, toilet, and bathroom). Regular water quality testing is conducted to ensure the water's safety. The construction of these grids is not technically complex and relies on locally sourced materials. The innovation lies in the entrepreneurial model employed, which operates within small clusters of households and involves local entrepreneurs who can co-invest. 

Max TapWater was a grant recipient of the Youth Co:Lab Bangladesh's Springboard programme 4.0, a collaborative initiative by the UNDP and Citi Foundation.

pads.title: Slow Sand Fiter
pads.snippet: Description: These filters are excellent for communities where there is no access to more efficient technologies. Through different layers of sand and gravel, the contaminants are filtered out through the final duct. It is important to emphasize that this type of filter is not effective for viruses, so other purification options should be considered beforehand.

pads.title: Description: It is a portable pasteurization device that combines solar and…
pads.snippet:
Description: It is a portable pasteurization device that combines solar and thermal energy. It consists of a 5-liter polythene bag with a clear plastic bubble lining on the front and black plastic on the back.

It is placed under direct sunlight, where pasteurization is achieved thanks to the incidence of solar rays on the black layer. AquaPak has an indicator on the cap that warns the user that the treatment is finished.

pads.title: Bio Sand Filter
pads.snippet: Description: It is a plastic container filled with sand and gravel, into which water is poured periodically. The biolayer of microorganisms that is created on the surface of the sand filters and removes pathogens from the water, which flows by hydrostatic pressure or siphon to a container of clean water. Sand and gravel are sourced locally.

pads.title: Membrane Filter
pads.snippet: Description: ROAMfilter Plus is a diaphragm filter with an intuitive design in the form of a bicycle pump. The filter cartridge has pores of size 0.02 μm. It is used by holding it with the feet and pumping with the handle to pass the water from the source through the filter and to the integrated tap. It can also be used in a gravity-driven installation. The device weighs 4.2 kg.

pads.title: Bucket and Candle Filter
pads.snippet:
Description: Similar to traditional filters such as the eco filter, but in this case the filtration is done by a "candle" that is horizontal. It is supplied without the water containers, which must be purchased locally. It can be purchased as a siphon kit, with a tube connected to the filter that channels the water to a drinking water container.

Very easy to use. Maintenance is performed by cleaning the candle periodically, this being the safety mechanism.

pads.title: Ozone Filter
pads.snippet: Description: Ozone filters are an excellent filtration method for communities that have access to piped water. It can be installed in a community center where people have access during certain hours of the day to filter water for consumption.

pads.title: Water Filter
pads.snippet: Description: Water for Life filters connect directly to the "jet" of the battery or any place where the water outlet is. Its filtration is almost immediate and protects people from diseases they can contract from drinking contaminated water.

pads.title: Filter Straw
pads.snippet: Description: It is a method to filter any type of water. The straw can filter from the water coming out of the jet, to water from river, lake or wells. It is ideal for communities that do not have access to piped water and the bodies of water to which they have access are contaminated.

pads.title: ECO Filter
pads.snippet: Description: ECOFILTRO is an ecological and aesthetic water purifier, dispenser and filter made from natural elements. Its filtration technology consists of: activated carbon, mud and colloidal silver. It is perfect for homes, workplaces or shared areas where water is needed for drinking.

pads.title: OLA Filter
pads.snippet:
Description: The OLA filter offers a solution for communities with access to a water source through pipes, but that is contaminated or unfit for human consumption. Through tiny fibers, all contaminants in the water are trapped.

It should only be connected to the outlet of the "Jet" and the water that comes out of the filter is completely filtered.

pads.title: Rice Husk
pads.snippet:
Description: Rice husk is a by-product of the milling industry, which is abundant in the rice areas of many countries and offers good properties to be used as a hydroponic substrate. Among its main properties are that it is an organic substrate with a low decomposition rate, it is light, good drainage, good aeration and its main cost is transportation.

The main drawback of rice husk is its low moisture retention capacity and how difficult it is to achieve a good distribution of it when used as a single substrate in hydroponic cultivation.

pads.title: Coconut Fiber
pads.snippet:
Description: Coconut fiber is a material that is extracted from coconuts, in order to reuse the organic matter that remains as waste when extracting the edible part of the coconut. It is very good for hydroponics as it retains moisture and is not compacted, which guarantees that there is oxygen, and that water circulates correctly throughout the crop.

Eventually it degrades and it is necessary to periodically change the substrate of hydroponic crops. One of the advantages of this product is that it can be obtained at a lower cost than other substrates, due to the fact of being extracted from a waste.

pads.title: Glass Stone
pads.snippet:
Description: This substrate is a 100% natural and recycled growth medium, perfect for vegetables, herbs and flowering plants. The spaces between the recycled glass "rocks" open up more oxygen to the plant roots, while the texture of the rock retains water without drowning the roots. This combination favors the development of the root, which translates into a better absorption of nutrients and water.

In addition, it is a lightweight material and does not dirty the media where it is used.

pads.title: Clay Pellets
pads.snippet:
Description: Fired clay pellets or granules are suitable for hydroponic systems in which all nutrients are carefully controlled in the aqueous solution. Clay granules have a neutral pH and do not contain any nutritional value.

The clay is formed into round granules and baked in rotary kilns. This causes the clay to expand, like popcorn, and become porous. It is lightweight and does not compact over time. The shape of each granule can be irregular or uniform, depending on the brand and manufacturing process.

pads.title: Solar Powered Food Dehydrator
pads.snippet: Solar powered fruit and vegetable dehydrator created on a nature-based farm in Dominica. The dehydrator is used to turn crops into alternative products such as banana flour, as well as to avoid food waste through preservation of the grown fruits and vegetables.

pads.title: ML subsea monitoring platform
pads.snippet: Bluemvmt changes the price/performance curve in the marine monitoring industry by providing a cost-effective hardware/software solution that combines an innovative subsea monitoring platform (SMP) allowing Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) to dock and upload data and recharge without needing to resurface. The data collected from the large array of sensors, hydrophones, acoustic modems, and cameras are uploaded in real-time to our Blue/AI Cloud. The software measures, tracks and reports on Land, Sea and Sky sensor streams and correlates them. The unique business model reduces their total cost of ownership for our customers over time through a unique revenue sharing program.

pads.title: Rock Wool
pads.snippet:
Description: Rock or mineral wool can retain large amounts of water and air that aid root growth and nutrient absorption in hydroponics; Its fibrous nature also provides a good mechanical structure to keep the plant stable. The naturally elevated pH of mineral wools makes them initially unsuitable for plant growth and requires "conditioning".

Rockwool is usually used only in the seedling phase or with freshly cut clones, but can remain with the base of the plant throughout its life.

pads.title: Run to Waste System
pads.snippet:
Description: In this system, nutrients are not recycled, but the plant receives a new mixture of nutrients constantly. The nutrients that have already been used are discarded by a final drain.

These systems typically use a substrate with a liquid retention similar to that of soil. That is, substrates maintain a high degree of humidity for a long period of time.

pads.title: Mist System
pads.snippet: Description: The system uses electric nebulizers (fog machines) that pump and vibrate under pressure to transform the mixture of nutrients and water into moisture, such as the humid atmosphere of a tropical or cloud area. This creates a constant moist, nutrient-rich fog for plant roots.

pads.title: Ebb and Flow System
pads.snippet:
Description: In an ebb and flow system, plant pots are temporarily flooded with nutrient solution and then drained back into the reservoir.

The flow is caused by a pump connected to a timer that is activated several times a day. When it stops working, the solution flows back into the tank.

pads.title: Drip Irrigation
pads.snippet: Description: In these irrigation systems, a timer controls a pump that causes the nutrient solution to drip onto the bottom of the plants. In some of these systems, it is possible to recover excess nutrient solution for reuse, while in others excess solution is discarded.

pads.title: Aeroponics System
pads.snippet: Description: Technique in which the roots are suspended in the air, within a dark medium, and watered with nutrient solution in frequency of a few minutes. Although it is a highly efficient technique, the roots can quickly dry out irrigation cycles are disrupted.

pads.title: Floating Root System
pads.snippet: Description: In this method, the plants are found in a sheet or raft – usually made of duroport – that floats on top of the nutrient solution, so that their roots are immersed within the solution. An air pump provides the roots with the oxygen necessary for their optimal development.

pads.title: NFT
pads.snippet:
Description: It is a technique where nutrients are pumped from a reservoir, and it is not necessary to manipulate plants.

This technique ensures the safety of the products, since it occurs inside large greenhouses that regulate the temperature and also protect crops from diseases or insects that may affect the crop.

pads.title: Gravity Irrigation
pads.snippet: Description: These irrigation systems work by taking advantage of the capacity of water to travel the path of the crop on its own. It does not need pumps and can be used to water your garden temporarily or throughout the season. It is also used in individual plants, orchards or row crops.

pads.title: Irrigation with vessels
pads.snippet:
Description: Millennial system that requires no energy and uses only the water that plants need. In addition, it employs artisans, contributes to food security, is cheap and biodegradable.

Through a system of transpiration, the vessels provide the necessary water to the plants that settle near them. The plants use the water they need and have a reserve at their fingertips, which allows them to reduce water stress in the dry season.

pads.title: Subterranean Drip Irrigation
pads.snippet:
Description: Underground drip irrigation is a method that involves applying water under the soil surface. To install this type of irrigation heavy machinery is necessary since several trenches need to be opened on the sides of the crops, in order to install pipes, pumps, etc. 

Through automated processes, the flow and amount of water that plants receive directly into the roots can be regulated.

pads.title: Sprinkler Irrigation
pads.snippet:
Description: The mechanism works through a network of pipes that transport water to the sprinklers, which use pressure to trigger it. Basically, it seeks to imitate the way in which rain would naturally irrigate these plants.

In this case, the implementation of this irrigation produced better quality potatoes and quadrupled the production compared to traditional irrigation.

pads.title: Drip Irrigation
pads.snippet: Description: This system is used in lavender plantations in Guadalajara and Cuenca. The system is ideal for this type of crops, since spraying of the aerial part of the plant is avoided, so that the flowers or leaves of the plant are not damaged.

pads.title: Collection Tanks for Schools
pads.snippet:
Description: The municipality of Guatemala, together with Global Water Partnership have developed these pilot systems as a solution for water scarcity in urban areas of Guatemala.

Like other collection systems, these are based on the collection of rain by gutters installed on the roof, which lead the water to tanks that serve to contain the water.

pads.title: Fog collectors
pads.snippet: Description: The Aqualonis system is easy to install and is carbon neutral, as it does not use energy for its operation. Through their ultra-thin high-tech meshes, they extract the water that is in the air and collect it in containers that store the liquid ensuring that the quality is optimal for human consumption.

pads.title: Water Collection tanks using the roof - Asucuch
pads.snippet: Description: The Association of Organizations of the Cuchumatanes has promoted this project as a measure of adaptation to climate change, focusing on the effects of droughts. The system they use captures the water through sheets of Aluzinc, then conducts the water into a PVC channel and finally settles inside a water tank. At the bottom is installed a multi connector that allows the extraction of water.

pads.title: Water Collection and Filtration Tanks
pads.snippet: Description: The way these systems work is through the installation of PVC collecting gutters on the edges of sheet roofs. These gutters conduct rainwater into a water tank, where the water is stored. Once the water is stored, the beneficiary families can open a tap, which allows the passage of water through a filter that purifies the liquid, for later consumption.

pads.title: Citizen science on Mapping of juvenile fish
pads.snippet: Contributory project: It is designed by members of the scientific community, and citizens participate in data collection.

pads.title: Pellet bioenergy
pads.snippet:
Pellet Mexico addresses the problems linked to reducing CO2 emissions, taking advantage of the energy potential of residual biomass and taking it as a substitute for fossil fuels.

Biomass is used for the renewable generation of thermal energy, also contributing to the proper management of forest, agricultural and organic waste.

pads.title: Biomaterials from pineapple
pads.snippet:
Substrato is a project that transforms agroindustrial waste into biomaterials that can be applied to developing sustainable products. This is achieved thanks to a multidisciplinary process that connects the field with creative and innovative methodologies and local knowledge and infrastructure.


This project was born as an academic exploration that arises from investigating and analyzing agro-industrial residues in Mexico to develop new alternatives for its use and management. This, in turn, implies the development of sustainable products that demonstrate the economic value of organic waste.


The research focused on pineapple leaves, the primary residue in producing this fruit, representing 75% of the harvested product. The waste that served as raw material for the project's development was obtained from Ciudad Isla, Veracruz, one of the key pineapple-producing states in Mexico.From the experiment, four biomaterials were developed (felt, bioplastic, chipboard, and rope), and some applications of the materials made of fiber and pineapple leaf bagasse.

pads.title: Ecolana, connecting with recycling companies
pads.snippet:
Ecolana is a Mexican startup is a platform that seeks to facilitate access to recycling, it has a map of recycling centers nationwide, to which the user has access.

Through the map, people can see more than 3,000 collection centers, find out the hours, the address and the type of material they receive.The founders Alejandra Valdez G and Lisseth Cordero started in 2016, when they realized that those who decided to recycle could not find a place to take the material.

In addition, recycling in Latin America is not so easy because there is no comprehensive waste management system. For this reason they took on the task of creating a database of the centers, which took them two years, because the compilation was done by hand and from door to door.

By 2018 the company built the first company and the business was consolidated. "What we do is connect this recycling chain, through technological tools."

pads.title: Satellite+AI Water quality monitoring
pads.snippet:
The project uses satellite imagery and artificial intelligence for automated analysis and constant monitoring of physical, chemical, and biological parameters such as:

• Surface temperature
• Turbidity
• Dissolved oxygen
• Chlorophyll-a
• Total nitrogen
• Total phosphorus

pads.title: Nejayote, biofuel and fertilizers
pads.snippet:
To produce maize tortillas, maize is first cooked with lime for 12-18 hours. Nejayote is the wastewater resulting from the process, a land pollutant. In Mexico, it is estimated that in 2012, 14.4 million cubic meters of Nejayote were produced per month. How to manage this waste is connected to how it can be better utilized.

The project seeks alternatives and methods that take advantage of the Nejayote for the production of energy and agricultural products by identifying the needs of a community and connecting with ways in which it can mitigate the Nejayote contamination problem and also a way in which it can help millers to profit from the waste they produce.

pads.title: Biorefinery with water lilies
pads.snippet:
Specialists from the Department of Biotechnology of the Iztapalapa Unit of the Autonomous Metropolitan University (UAM) designed a biorefinery for the sustainable management of water lilies in the Xochimilco canals in the south of Mexico City.

 The installation can be adapted to different topographies, replicated, and scaled in other sites, according to parameters of environmentally friendly technology, social justice, and economic viability. Dr. Ernesto Favela Torres –responsible for the project– has been working for over 40 years in research to use the plant as an absorbent for water purification in rivers and canals.

pads.title: Lombri Compost Service
pads.snippet: Collection of household organic waste in zones 1 and 2 of Guatemala City. The waste is collected for composting, for a price of Q.60.00 per month and collection is carried out once a week.

pads.title: InProtein
pads.snippet: They propose more efficient and environmentally sound ways to meet this rapidly growing population's food and nutritional needs. Through insect protein, Inprotin seeks to meet these needs in an innovative way.

pads.title: BeeHub
pads.snippet: It is one of the few honey productions where the practices are focused on the care of the bees and their natural cycles. In addition to production, they focus on creating consumer awareness.

pads.title: Masking tape identification
pads.snippet: Through identification with masking tape and colored markers, the bags can be differentiated depending on the type of waste they contain.

pads.title: LEED certifications in shopping centre
pads.snippet: The shopping centre "Naranjo Mall" is certified under the LEED statutes, which are a series of guidelines that help the place to be more environmentally friendly. Among the things that the place must carry out, is the improvement of the recycling and solid waste system.

pads.title: Plastic Bag Strips
pads.snippet: This basic solution is an inexpensive and accessible way to identify your waste bags with different colours, in order to facilitate the sorting of solid waste.

pads.title: Uber Moto
pads.snippet: Affordable and reliable mobility option for users and an alternative for driver-partners who want to generate additional income. This option is a new alternative that gives driver-partners with a motorbike the same benefits in schedule flexibility, while maintaining the safety standard of the Uber app.

pads.title: Electric Scooters
pads.snippet: The new scooters in Guatemala offer a comfortable, fast, light and ecological transport service. They are part of the company Wayfree, representative of the Californian firm Bird, which has the support of Bantrab to introduce the leasing of electric scooters in the country.

pads.title: Electric Buses
pads.snippet: This project seeks to expand public transport routes, putting electric buses into circulation to reduce the environmental impact of journeys. The line will be 12 kilometres long and is intended to benefit 40,000 users, according to the mayor's estimate.

pads.title: Solar Tuk Tuk
pads.snippet:
This is the Tuk Tuk Solar 2021, a project promoted by the G-22 Environmental Association and the Biciudad Movement to promote the use of renewable energies, analyse the current transport model and at the same time generate a national unity project.

It is a form of transport that uses solar and electric energy.

pads.title: Alternative taxis
pads.snippet: Using a private car without any permit or special identification as taxis, many people use their vehicles to offer transport services in areas with a high influx of informal and formal workers. Fares are cheap and are shared with other transport users.

pads.title: mixed recycling transport
pads.snippet: As there is a need for economical and efficient transport of recycled materials, a system has been devised whereby owners of pickup trucks and other vehicles used to carry other items such as vegetables or materials can carry recycling material when they are no longer loaded.

pads.title: Integrated Solid Waste Management: IRTRA
pads.snippet: The IRTRA is an excellent example of good solid waste management. Through their management, they convert organic waste into compost for their gardens and try to recycle the vast majority of inorganic waste.

pads.title: Water and Soils for Agriculture (ASA)
pads.snippet: The project seeks to implement practices such as planting certain species and using organic fertilisers alongside traditional maize and bean crops to retain rainwater, which is falling more and more irregularly. They are currently working in arid areas of Guatemala.

pads.title: New Wheelchair: freedom to move around
pads.snippet: With the help of undergraduates and international design collaborators, Amos Winter a mechanical engineering, has designed a wheelchair device that can carry users comfortably and efficiently off-road. The device it's intended to help people in countries where the access to wheelchairs is limited, but also where the rough terrain and the long distance travels are a limitation. It is small and maneuverable indoors too. Given the need to have a wheelchair that can move through rocky and muddy paths, the Leveraged Freedom Chair (LFC) performs like a combination of a desk chair and a mountain bike. The deviced has been tested with the people that would use it to make sure it's efficient and useful. The LFC it's now to be prototyped and tested with 30 persons in Guatemala.

pads.title: Vertmonde: reciclaje de E-Waste
pads.snippet: El manejo inadecuado de residuos eléctricos y electrónicos resultan altamente contaminantes para las personas y el Medioambiente. Vertmonde realiza una gestión adecuada de estos residuos, contribuyendo al consumo ético y sostenible de tecnología: se reduce la contaminación ambiental, se evitan problemas de salud y se protegen recursos naturales. Su programa de reciclaje especializado ofrece servicios tanto para hogares como para empresas, instituciones públicas, fabricantes e importadores. Además, a través de su servicio Vertmonde Box ofrecen servicio a domicilio para recoger residuos electrónicos.

pads.title: World and Recycler: Chatarra electrónica en Ecuador
pads.snippet: La empresa World and Recycler, creada en Guayaquil, se encarga de destruir definitivamente dispositivos en estado de chatarra electrónica contribuyendo así con el cuidado del Medioambiente. La empresa adquiere, recolecta, acopia y reclasifica equipos electrónicos que, una vez que han cumplido su vida útil, resultan altamente tóxicos para las personas y tienen un impacto ambiental negativo. Mediante la compra o a partir de donaciones que reciben, entregan Certificados de Destrucción del material contaminante, asegurando que los materiales se han trabajado de una manera ambientalmente adecuada.

pads.title: Offline-Pedia: contenido académico de calidad para zonas rurales y sin acceso a internet
pads.snippet: Joshua Salazar, estudiante de la Universidad Yachay, ha sido premiado por ser uno de los innovadores menores de 35 años en Latinoamérica. Con su proyecto Offline-Pedia, pensado para reducir la brecha de conectividad. Así, en zonas rurales en las cuales no hay acceso a internet fijo o móvil, las personas pueden acceder a contenido académico de calidad. Mediante la combinación de materiales reciclados, Joshua ha aportado en la instalación de computadores baratos en cuatro comunidades rurales de Ecuador. El uso de una placa que contiene el software libre Kiwix, permite el acceso a sitios web como Wikipedia, sin conexión a internet. Este innovador está buscando financiamiento para poder convertir este proyecto en una ONG que permita llevar la Offline-Pedia a más zonas rurales del país.

pads.title: Biol: abono orgánico para nutrir cultivos
pads.snippet: El Instituto Nacional Autónomo de Investigaciones Agropecuarias en convenio con el Gobierno Provincial de Santo Domingo de los Tsáchilas presentan una alternativa orgánica para nutrir y desarrollar los cultivos de la zona. Con el objetivo de promover y estimular el desarrollo de las plantas (follaje, raíces y floración), en la Estación Experimental de Santo Domingo (INIAP), se preparó de manera fácil esta mezcla de estiércol y otros materiales orgánicos que son ingresados en un tanque que posteriormente se sella dejando una manguera que permite la salida de gases. De esta manera se consigue un producto sencillo de realizar que aportará a los programas de nutrición de los cultivos.

pads.title: Catálogo: 100 hierbas medicinales
pads.snippet: El Proyecto Territorios que Sanan, el Museo de la Ciudad y la Plataforma Primero de Mayo, con el apoyo técnico del PNUD, busca revalorizar el trabajo de hierbateras del mercado de San Roque, considerando su aporte en la conservación de ecosistemas y en el cuidado de la salud de la ciudadanía. Como parte de la Minga de Innovación del PNUD y con apoyo de estudiantes de la Escuela de Formación de Tecnólogos de la Escuela Politécnica Nacional, se realizaron varios prototipos para dar solución a problemáticas que enfrentan las hierbateras de la Plataforma. Además, se realizó este catálogo, que esta en construcción permanente, y es una estrategia para conservar los saberes ancestrales que al ser transmitidos de forma empírica y verbal corren el riesgo de no seguir en oficio debido al relevo generacional.

pads.title: Sistema de riego automático
pads.snippet: Como parte de la Minga de Innovación del Laboratorio de Aceleración PNUD, y con el fin de encontrar soluciones a problemáticas que enfrentan las hierbateras de la Plataforma Primero de Mayo en el mercado de San Roque. Estudiantes de la ESFOT de la Escuela Politécnica Nacional identificaron que una de las problemáticas está relacionada con la carencia de un sistema de riego para abastecer los sembríos de forma eficiente. Por esto, realizaron un prototipo de sistema de riego por aspersión automatizado que usa un sensor de humedad y una bomba, para poder facilitar el acceso del agua a los sembríos, así como evitar que las hierbateras tengan que movilizar el agua de manera mecánica haciendo grandes esfuerzos físicos. De esta forma, además, se aprovecha de mejor manera el agua, evitando desperdicios.

pads.title: Popular market composting
pads.snippet:
According to data from the Quito Informa Agency of July 2023, the city generates an average of 2,300 tons of waste per day, only 1% of which is recovered by waste pickers who work under extremely precarious conditions to gather PET bottles, tetrapacks, plastic, cardboard, and other waste. Meanwhile, 60% of all waste is compostable material that comes from households, businesses, and markets. San Roque is one of the main reception areas for the indigenous peoples who have been expelled from the countryside since the 70s, so it has been a key tie to rural-urban linkage. In the very same complex, the Primero de Mayo Central Market has operated since January 15, 1975, bringing together more than 150 traders of which more than 100 are herbalists engaged in the production, collection, and sale of edible and medicinal herbs. This market is the first link in the distribution of medicinal herbs in the city, as it supplies intermediary traders from other markets in the sector and in the city. However, wholesale does not yield an advantage or higher profit. In fact, more than 85% of these producers earn less than minimum wage. Price ceilings are imposed by intermediaries, who increase the final price by up to 200%. 


In this context, in 2022, the UNDP Ecuador Acceleration Lab coordinated a 'Community Innovation Minga,' which consists in co-creating and testing solutions s to address challenges faced by medicinal herb vendors at the Primero de Mayo Central Market in Quito, together with students from the National Polytechnic University’s Vocational Training School. As a result of several months of collaboration, 31 ideas were devised, of which 5 turned into functional prototypes and four were piloted, one of them related to organic waste management. We now know that the problem of organic waste management can be turned into an opportunity through a circular economy model. Throughout 2023, the Primero de Mayo Central Market, with the support of Ecuador´s Accelerator Lab, the Faculty of Civil and Environmental Engineering of the National Polytechnic School, and  'Marca Patito' enterprise implemented the pilot project for organic waste management with a circular economy approach to compost organic waste for both commercialization and personal use by the traders. Below, we present this pilot's results and lessons learned.

pads.title: Destiladora artesanal de plantas medicinales
pads.snippet: Como parte de la Minga de Innovación del Laboratorio de Aceleración PNUD, y con el fin de encontrar soluciones a problemáticas que enfrentan las yerbateras de la Plataforma Primero de Mayo en el mercado de San Roque, estudiantes de la ESFOT de la Escuela Politécnica Nacional han desarrollado un prototipo de destiladora artesanal que permite evitar el desecho de la excedencia de plantas medicinales. Esta destiladora permite obtener aceites esenciales y agua perfumada, los cuales tienen un buen valor comercial.

pads.title: Prototipo de Horno Solar para Secado de plantas
pads.snippet: Este prototipo surge como parte de la Minga de Innovación comunitaria, coordinada por el Laboratorio de Aceleración del PNUD, para la co-creación y testeo de soluciones para abordar desafíos de las comerciantes de hierbas medicinales de la Plataforma Central Primero de Mayo en Quito. Los estudiantes de la ESFOT de la Escuela Politécnica Nacional, son los innovadores de este deshidratador solar, que cuenta con varios niveles para secar la excedencia de producto de hierbas medicinales y así evitar varios problemas derivados de esa excedencia, tanto económicos como de salud. Si bien las condiciones climáticas ideales resultarán en un secado más rápido, el prototipo ha demostrado ser útil en condiciones adversas también.

pads.title: "Bombas de semilla" para restaurar suelos de baja fertilidad
pads.snippet: Estas bombas, inspiradas en la técnica japonesa "nendo dango", son una estrategia útil para recuperar zonas en cuyo suelo no han funcionado las técnicas restaurativas convencionales. El FONAG, en su Programa de Recuperación de la Cobertura Vegetal, busca  favorecer la restauración del Área de Conservación Hídrica Antisana con esta técnica.

pads.title: Biofiltros para el tratamiento de aguas residuales
pads.snippet: La comunidad de Chilcapamba, en colaboración con el FONAG y el grupo Yakunina,construyeron un biofiltro para tratar aguas negras y grises, en una de las casas de la localidad. Esta comunidad no cuenta con alcantarillado adecuado para el desecho de aguas residuales, lo cual convierte este tipo de biofiltros en una de las alternativas más viables en cuanto a tecnología ecológica. Al pasar por el vermifiltro de lombrices, el agua cumple con los índices de calidad adecuados para ser enviada el río.

pads.title: Agave for land restoration and cattle feed
pads.snippet:
Agave plants and nitrogen-fixing trees can reduce and isolate considerable amounts of CO2. They also produce more biomass above and below ground on a continuous basis than any other desert or semi-desert species.
It is estimated that this system can absorb and store the dry weight equivalent of 30-50 tons of CO2/ha/year both above and below ground.

Currently the use of agave for land restoration is promoted by the Billion Agaves Project, which is an ecosystem regeneration strategy adopted by innovative Mexican farms located in the high desert region of Guanajuato. This strategy combines the growth of agave plants and nitrogen-fixing companion forest species (such as mesquite), with rotational grazing of cattle. The result is a high biomass, high forage production system that works well even on degraded semi-arid lands. The system produces large quantities of agave leaves and pineapples, up to a ton of biomass during the 8 to 10 years of the plant's life. When chopped and fermented in closed containers, the agave leaf makes excellent animal fodder and is cheap (2 cents a pound). This agroforestry system reduces overgrazing pressure on fragile pastures and improves soil health and water retention while reducing and storing enormous amounts of atmospheric CO2. The goal of the Billion Agaves campaign is to plant one billion agaves around the world to reduce and store billions of tons of CO2 that destabilize the climate. The campaign will be sponsored by donations and public and private investments.

pads.title: Recycled polystyrene waterproofing
pads.snippet: Economical liquid composite waterproofing based on recycled polystyrene, which can be easily applied with a roller or brush, capable of adhering to multiple surfaces, with a performance equal to or better than its competitors, but with better thermal, optical and mechanical properties. It has the capacity to cover up to 2 m2 per liter of product and is also capable of perfectly sealing cracks up to 1.5 mm wide for a period of more than 8 months, according to our most recent studies. The product was improved with additives that, according to various analyses, reflects 99.9% of UV radiation (which is the main cause of polystyrene degradation), as well as being flame retardant and reflecting more than 90% of infrared light, which , as a whole, the temperature difference between exterior and interior decreases by more than 20 °C, even in extremely hot conditions, such as in the Yucatan Peninsula. Given its reliability, reinforcing mesh is not required, which further reduces the installation cost, and can be applied by anyone without high technical knowledge and using minimal personal protection equipment.

pads.title: aquaponic drip system
pads.snippet: In these irrigation systems, a timer controls a pump that causes the nutrient solution to drip onto the underside of the plants. In some of these systems, it is possible to recover excess nutrient solution for reuse, while in others the excess solution is discarded.

pads.title: Ebb and flow system
pads.snippet: An ebb and flow system temporarily floods the growing trays with nutrient solution and then drains the nutrient solution back into the reservoir. The flow is triggered by a pump connected to a timer that is activated several times a day. When the timer stops running, the solution flows back into the reservoir.

pads.title: Aeroponics System
pads.snippet: A technique in which the roots are suspended in air, in a dark medium, and are misted with nutrient solution every few minutes. Although it is a highly efficient technique, roots can dry out quickly if misting cycles are interrupted.

pads.title: Root System Floating
pads.snippet: In this method, the plants are placed in a sheet or raft - usually made of unicell - that floats on top of the nutrient solution, so that their roots are submerged in the solution. An air pump provides the roots with the oxygen necessary for optimal development.

pads.title: Nutrient film system
pads.snippet: It consists of creating a recirculating film of nutrient solution. The nutrient solution is pumped from a reservoir into growth trays or PVC tubes with plants, where it comes into contact with their roots before returning to the reservoir.

pads.title: Wick system
pads.snippet:
His technique is one of the simplest, as it does not require pumps to transport the nutrient solution from the reservoir to the growing trays. Instead, the plants receive the nutrient solution via wicks or wicks.

It can only be used for plants that require little water.

pads.title: Irrigation with pots
pads.snippet: An ancient system that requires no energy and uses only the water the plants need. It also provides employment for artisans, contributes to food security, is cheap and biodegradable.

pads.title: Underground drip irrigation
pads.snippet: Subsurface drip irrigation is a method of applying water below the soil surface. This is done by using buried micro-pipes. The strategy of this type of irrigation is to apply very small amounts of water with a high frequency. This ensures constant moisture in the soil.

pads.title: Sprinkler irrigation
pads.snippet: It consists of applying water by imitating rain, i.e. by means of a jet of water sprayed in droplets. The mechanism works through a network of pipes that transports the water to the sprinklers, which use pressure to trigger it.

pads.title: Gravity irrigation
pads.snippet: These irrigation systems work by harnessing the ability of water to travel the path of least resistance on its own. It does not require pumps and can be used to water your garden temporarily or throughout the season. It is also used for individual plants, orchards or row crops.

pads.title: Drip irrigation
pads.snippet: Irrigation method used in arid areas as it allows the optimal use of water and fertilizers. The water applied by this method of irrigation infiltrates towards the roots of the plants, directly irrigating the zone of influence of the roots through a system of pipes and emitters, which increases productivity and yields.

pads.title: Ozone filters (O3)
pads.snippet: Ozone filters (O3) are an excellent choice for homes or places such as offices, schools or meeting centers. Through the ozonation process, water for human consumption is filtered.

pads.title: SunSpring Hybrid
pads.snippet: SunSpring Hybrid is an autonomous microbiological water purification system, powered by solar and wind energy, capable of producing up to 20,000 liters per day for more than 10 years.

pads.title: FoliaWater
pads.snippet: a book whose pages kill microbes in water. The product originates from Dankovich's doctoral thesis, which focused on the development of paper filters with silver nanoparticles that kill bacteria, viruses and other pathogens. This filter allows thousands of families to have access to clean drinking water on a daily basis.

pads.title: Water 4 life
pads.snippet: Water 4 Life Global is working on different projects related to water in Lake Atitlán. One of these projects is their water filters, which they donate to the communities so that people can filter their water and consume it without risk of disease.

pads.title: Lifestraw
pads.snippet: All LifeStraw products start with advanced hollow fibre membrane technology. These are fibre bundles with microscopic holes, so small that organisms such as bacteria, parasites and even dirt and microplastics cannot pass through them. This solution puts pure water within reach of your pocket.

pads.title: Sunny Clean Water
pads.snippet: Solar stills for water purification have been used in the Americas since pre-Columbian times. The technique is simple: water is evaporated using solar energy and the vapour condenses on a surface to collect the clean water.

pads.title: BubbleTech
pads.snippet: Through a system of mass transfer and elimination of contaminants through bubbles. This system can filter water and air with a purification efficiency of 99.98% and the use of 98% of the water. It is ideal for treating saline, waste and industrial water.

pads.title: EcoFilter
pads.snippet: El Ecofiltro es capaz de purificar el agua de casi cualquier fuente (de pila, pozo, grifo, río, lago laguna o lluvia, etc.), con muy pocas excepciones, como por ejemplo el agua salada del mar. Es una excelente solución para comunidades en donde la calidad del agua no es la adecuada.

pads.title: Ola Filter
pads.snippet: The system uses a tight loop of hollow fibre membranes with microscopic pores that block bacteria, parasites, cysts, micro plastics and sediments in order to filter drinking water. This is an excellent solution for communities with no access to safe drinking water and expensive to buy.

pads.title: AquaLonis - water collecting nets
pads.snippet: Each collector net is quick and easy to install and requires no maintenance. The collectors are carbon neutral, as they operate without energy. The system produces high quality drinking water (approved by WHO standards) and can provide water for agriculture and forestry.

pads.title: Solar boats for the Amazon

Their goal is to provide clean infrastructure to support technological independence, while liberating communities from the restraints of gasoline power. In the Amazon, geographical dispersion demands the use of gasoline-run boats or canoes, at very high prices. Therefore, solar energy implementation (e.g.solar powered boats) can reduce dependencies on petrol and money.

pads.title: Healthy habits for healthy environment
pads.snippet: The vast majority of the citizens of Skopje live in areas that do not meet the minimum air quality standards, mainly caused by heavy vehicle use. Skopje citizens also face disruptive public transport with lack of real time monitoring tools in most of the areas. Walking and cycling as methods of commuting have the potential to decrease vehicle use, thus can be attained by diverting motorized commuting for distance of 2 km to walking; and for distance of 5 km to bicycle commuting, by promoting healthy and active lifestyle. Namely, daily walking and cycling have various health benefits, including cardiovascular and muscular endurance, body weight control, lowered blood pressure etc. In addition, other benefits include low costs, energy efficiency, time saving during the peak period of urban traffic, and reduced noise pollution. The overall aim regarding fluctuating urban mobility is to encourage and motivate individuals (aged 18 - 65) to practice efficient mobility i.e. to walk or to use pedal or/electric bicycles, whilst altering their daily activity patterns in terms of costs, energy and environmental conservation. We influenced behavioral changes in terms of mobility by focusing on test group consisted of 50 citizens, which perceptions and behaviors were be measured before, during and after the challenges. How we did it? - Our innovative approach for citizens’ mobilization was with one of the highly rated sport/activity application-STRAVA App. The application is used to measure people’s sports activities - hiking, running, walking, cycling, swimming etc. It uses GPS, thus gives precise calculations on the speed and distance, and additionally, it calculates statistical data over periods of time (daily, weekly, monthly). If connected with smart watch, the app goes deeper in the statistics and calculates the stress level, heartbeat, pulse ox and more. It offers users to join group challenges but it also allows creation of custom made challenges - the option that we used. We created 2 group challenges – one for walking (up to 2 km daily), other for cycling (up to 6 km daily) and randomized the test group members into them. All group participants could see who reached the challenge goal and beyond, thus there was strong competitiveness among them. After the challenges ended, we calculated and checked whether all participants reached the goals. The ones that did not were disqualified, while the others were rewarded with sport equipment. The ones that went beyond the challenge got an extra reward. The pre and post research showed that people change daily habits with small incentives.  92% of the test group walking - finished the challenge, from which 65% will continue walking that distance on daily basis. 84% of the test group cycling finished the challenge, from which 61% will continue this practice on daily basis.  People get extra motivation if a target is set and got competitive when are part of a bigger group. In addition, they were motivated by their engagement in the policy making process. This action also encapsulated participatory approach by providing comments and suggestions on improving the quality of urban mobility infrastructure and sending them to the relevant authorities.

pads.title: Biocompost- external service
pads.snippet:
In Quito, around 2,000 to 2,400 tons of garbage are generated daily. That means that every 2 months we Quiteños can fill the Atahualpa Olympic Stadium with garbage. Likewise, the production of garbage in the city continues to grow exponentially.

 

More than half of the garbage we generate is organic waste and it can be easily decomposed. That is, they do not need large amounts of energy to transform. Despite this, they are a source of pollution since if they are not used correctly they produce methane (CH4), which is 25 times more polluting than carbon dioxide (CO2).

 

Quito lacks an effective treatment for the management of organic waste. This solution was found when ideating about how herbalists could increase their livelihoods and use their surplus medicinal plants in a way that it didn´t get wasted. Composting is an interesting alternative, but for them, it requires transportation from the market to their plots to compost and time, which is very scarce. Outsourcing their organic waste may be a more viable alternative, and in return they would get a valuable material so needed for their orchards.

pads.title: Coconut shell bricks
pads.snippet:
As part of a research thesis, innovator has developed a brick prototype using cocoa husks and mud, for construction use  in Bucay canton, located in Guayas, Ecuador. Several tests have been carried out so that the materials meet the necessary requirements demanded by construction regulations. Farmers from  Bucay discard cocoa shells, since they are only interested in marketing its nut; while the mud is used for the manufacture of handicrafts. The problem is trying to address is the fact that the residential constructions of the sector use materials such as cane and wood and this brick can offer a non-polluting and sustainable construction solution to people with limited resources as well as livelihoods.

pads.snippet: Market vendors reduce the usage of plastic by making bags out of coconut leaves.

pads.title: iNaturalistEc
pads.snippet:
iNaturalist is a citizen science app that promotes the culture of observation, registration and dissemination of biodiversity, and promotes the National Biodiversity Database (BNDB). With this platform it will be possible to learn more about the life cycles, distribution and population dynamics of all the species that inhabit our country.

Any interested nature lover who wishes to learn more about Ecuador's biodiversity can participate using this citizen science tool, thus contributing to the strengthening of scientific research.

pads.title: Water biofilters
pads.snippet: Estas jardineras se realizan con un vermifiltro. El vermifiltro es uno de los mejores inventos de las últimas dos décadas en relación al tratamiento descentralizado de aguas negras. Es un sistema aeróbico, la descomposición de la materia orgánica está realizada principalmente por lombrices (eisenia foetida), bacterias y otros microorganismos aeróbicos cuyo principal subproducto es humus. El mantenimiento de estos sistemas es simple y solo requiere un cambio de sustrato una vez al año.

pads.title: Accesible orchads
pads.snippet:
Huertos de altura es una solución para personas con movilidad reducida, tanto de la tercera edad como personas con discapacidad. Permite el acceso a la huerta de forma ergonómica. Mantiene a las personas activas en sus hobbies. Se trata de un diseño inclusivo que se ha puesto en práctica en la provincia de Jujuy.
Esta práctica fue mapeada en Ecuador en el 2019, con otro fin, que era mantener a los cultivos libres de inundación en el caso de la provincia de Esmeraldas.
Los huertos elevados por tanto son soluciones ergonómicas pero también resilientes a zonas con exceso de lluvia.

pads.snippet: Arunima Malik, Coen Bongers, Bonnie McBain.

pads.title: DIY Repurposing Project - Wheel Rim Stove
pads.snippet: Most of these old rims often find their way into landfills, but this household has turned it into something new and innovative. More communities located on the maritime and in semi/rural areas are finding out the enjoyment of cooking outdoors. Not only does it cut costs, but it also reduces the consumption of nonrenewable. This innovation is the perfect project for the "Do It Yourself" building crowd ...

pads.title: Using Stone Walls as a Multipurpose Climate Change Adaptation Tool
pads.snippet: Retaining walls help to enhance overall property value, they are durable and low maintenance, and extremely functional. Stone walls are eco-friendly and optimal because they use minimal space and prevent soil erosion during natural disasters such as flooding. Not only is it used to protect or enhance the value of a property but the most common types of stone walls are used in interior design such as limestone and sandstone.

pads.title: Local Restaurant uses Natural Materials for Shelter
pads.snippet: Thatch roofing is renewable, available, and quite durable.  It provides excellent insulation and keeps the room in the hot times. In addition, the superb insulation enables the restaurant to save on electricity for heating and cooking. They are much more environmentally friendly than shingles, which are made of metal and can be recycled and reused as shingles on the roofs.

pads.title: Broadband Satellite Technology bridges Digital Divide
pads.snippet: 3 Link Communication uses broadband satellite technology manufactured by Boeing and launched by SpaceX. The internet connectivity service is powered by a generation geostationary satellite that operates in the Ka-band frequency spectrum. It has a wide coverage that extends to over 25 countries reaching many islands, mountainous and rural regions. Coverage is everywhere in Vanuatu...

pads.title: Used Shipping Containers Transformed into Classrooms
pads.snippet: School in Vanuatu upcycles shipping containers into classrooms. Container classrooms are practical and safe solutions for students and can be used in all climatic conditions due to their effective insulation and cooling capability. The cost is also significantly lower than building a permanent concrete structure.

pads.title: Hand Crafted Artisan Chocolate
pads.snippet: Aelan means "Island" in Bislama, the language of Vanuatu. Aelan Chocolate Makers was born from a passion for cocoa and artisanal manufacturing. The business is based in Vanuatu and uses hand-farmed cocoa that is locally grown. The chocolate bars are infused with a variety of flavors such as Turmeric, Chili pepper, ginger, sea salt, Coconut, Nangai, Coffee and Cocoa nibs.

pads.title: Market Vendor Lauds Biogas Benefits
pads.snippet: Two biogas units were installed at the Port Vila City market house to supply methane gas to the food vendors at the food vendors. This biogas is sourced from horse manure that was brought in by the Department of Agriculture and Rural Development several months ago. The waste from biogas production is a liquid that vendors use around the market house as a source of fertilizer. Some of the market vendors also use this in their gardens.

pads.title: Local market vendor upcycles plastic to make bags and baskets
pads.snippet: A local market vendor sells bags and baskets made out of upcycling plastic. Vanuatu has a world-leading single-use plastic ban that came into effect in 2018, banning non-biodegradable plastic including bags and polystyrene containers. Upcycling plastic uses minimal natural resources and saves plastic waste from ending up in landfills.

pads.title: Local market vendor uses natural materials to make bags and baskets
pads.snippet: Utilizing traditional knowledge to make bags and baskets out of natural materials is a common practice for SMEs in Pacific island states. As illustrated below, a local market vendor sells bags and baskets with unique designs and patterns.

pads.title: Local health centers utilize solar cells to generate electricity
pads.snippet: By utilizing solar cells/panels, this health center is decreasing its emissions and in the long run is contributing to a greener future. Another benefit to this is it reduces electricity bills and is suitable for remote areas that are not connected to energy grids.

pads.title: Traditional fishing using local canoe
pads.snippet: Fishing canoes although common in PICs are useful for navigating lakes, rivers because of their size, they are easy to transport. Another reason this practice is still used till date is the orginal concept behind it. Wooden canoes signify the interest of protecting the local fishing culture and sentiments of the indigenous.

pads.snippet: Disposal of baby diapers is wrapped up tightly and separated from other solid wastes in the house.

A key feature of this initiative is the way it will provide technical assistance to strengthen the capacity of local communities while also establishing a climate project financing facility within FDB.

pads.title: Rain Collection System
pads.snippet:
In Skopje, the average annual precipitation in 2020 was about 600 mm, so a roof with 100 m2 can collect an average of 60,000 l of water.

Keeping this in mind, the students of Vlado Tasevski want to reduce the use of potable water for irrigation of the areas around the school.

Collecting and using rainwater in underground containers that they will use to water their own plants in the school yard.

All the equipment that will be installed would also have a permanent application in the implementation of the Hydrotechnics subject taught in the mechanical engineering school in the 2nd, 3rd and 4th year.

pads.title: Water well System
pads.snippet:
The high-school "Brakja Miladinovci" from Skopje, will reduce the consumption of drinking water, for irrigation and maintenance of the school yard and the zoo by renewing the school well.

1. Installation of a pipeline to the yard and to the drinking fountain, where electronic drinking fountains will be installed.

2. Building a drip-by-drip system for garden plantings.

3. Construction of a transparent mini water purification station from natural materials.

pads.title: Community School Water Project
pads.snippet: For the first time, villagers of Kade on Koro islands now have access to clean and safe drinking water. This was all thanks to the funding donated by the EU, Rotary Pacific Water for Life Foundation, and co-financing by the Rural Maritime Development Ministry, VaiWai Natural Artesian Waters, and Latter-day Saints Charities.

pads.title: DIY Composting Module
pads.snippet: A ‘compo-station’ that converts organic waste into compost while producing high-quality fertilizer. The vermicompost is made of three 19-liter buckets cut into three different heights to create separate levels. The first is where fresh remains directly from the kitchen are placed. the second, holds a variety of red wigglers, white and other earthworms acting as a transition space made of bio-refuse mixed with other bedding materials. The final stage holds a collection of leachate, a liquid that is used in the process for top-dressing development. The workstation is made of standard sized pieces of lumber and of 12mm plywood.

pads.title: Biomaterials to replace disposable food packaging
pads.snippet:
The project "Malteria" seeks to provide a solution to the problem caused by the massive consumption of disposables in informal food stalls by proposing the replacement of two essential elements in this food sale, a plate for solid food and a bag, both made with biomaterials using as principal material the same waste produced by this sector prevails, such as the corn husks of the tamales, which are also biodegradable.

This project is a collaboration of Taina Campos with Cointya Oviedo.

pads.title: Knowledge Transfer of Sustainable Organic Practices
pads.snippet: The village of Abaca is home to Fiji's national heritage park - Koroyanitu National Heritage Park and is site of attraction for tourists. The village is abundant in natural resources however farmers lack knowledge of sustainable organic practices and this is where the Foundation for Rural Integrated Enterprises & Development (FRIEND) have stepped in.

pads.title: Waste Segregation at Mana Coffee
pads.snippet: Mana Coffee is a 3-in-1 - café, kava bar and BnB in Suva, Fiji.  This restaurant is very popular among local residents and also helps in supporting other SMEs by selling their products.

pads.title: Multi-Nutrients mineral blocks and Pelletes for livestock
pads.snippet: Dr. Nambi from Makerere University College of Agriculture and Environmental Science mix multinutritional feeds to make blocks and pellets for livestock for enhanced productivity.

pads.title: Azoverm: A slow release nano-formulated organic soil amendment to restore fertility and nutrients
pads.snippet: This solution is by researchers at Makerere University who used Azolla blended with verniculite nanoparticles to restore soil fertility through balancing the PH, improve organic matter content as well as allowiing slow release of nutrients to plants which minimizes leakages to the environment.

pads.title: Smart O' ou jardin smart
"Jara foone" Connected wristband
pads.snippet: This solution based on the NFC technology inserted on a traditional wristband will help have all the information to find and save a missed child. The solution makes it possible to prevent the short or long disappearance of children, a phenomenon that is quite widespread in Senegal. The child wears this very harmless bracelet which will help find him very quickly when it is necessary.

pads.title: "Penccum Ndokh" Restaurer la biodiversité et la nature sur une décharge
pads.snippet: La solution consiste en une transformation radicale d'une vielle décharge sauvage de 20 ans en un espace public de revitalisation de la biodiversité que la population utilise pour se détendre, se réunir ou organiser des événements. Avec le soutien de jeunes bénévoles, la décharge installée sur une partie d'une vallée asséchée, a été nettoyée pendant au moins trois ans avant d'être restaurée dans son état actuel. Les oiseaux et les poissons ont déjà commencé à reconquérir l’espace aquatique.

pads.title: MRI Uganda: locally constructed MRI for Babies with hydrocephalus
pads.snippet: Mbarara University of Science and Technology Biomedical Engineers designed a low-Field Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) machine that is said to be the preferred diagnostic method for infant hydrocephalus. This is low-cost MRI technology is under development by reducing the strength of the magnetic field and the use of alternative technologies to create the magnetic field which is cheaper in terms of cost and uses less power. The final design was validated by stakeholders from the Ugandan Healthcare Authorities.

pads.title: Microgreens Fiji
pads.snippet: Nazeem Nisha (Innovator) is the founder of Microgreens Fiji. Like many others, Nazeem lost her job due to the pandemic in 2020. As a single parent she found it very difficult to cope and so decided to apply for assistance under the innovation project funded by the Australian government. With this innovation of hers, Nazeem grows a mixture of fenugreek, mustard, radish, and beetroot packs and already has an established market selling to hotels in Nadi and on the outer islands, high-end cuisine restaurants, and individuals on a weekly basis.

pads.title: World's Biggest Baby Incubator that carries 10 babies in one go
Vunilagi Book Club
pads.snippet: Vunilagi Book Club (VBC) is a learning platform that promotes book reading in rural communities in and around Fiji. Many children living in communities with lower socioeconomic backgrounds struggle with literacy skills. The club holds reading sessions in Nanuku - a community on the outskirts of Suva (Fiji's capital). VBC also finds ways to incorporate literacy skills via creative activities to enable children to see the benefits of reading as a skill. It is also the first to target children's literacy skills in underserved communities.

pads.title: Coastal Seawall
pads.snippet: A local community in the Western Province of the Solomon Islands has adapted to the effects of climate change. Due to the rise in sea level, the roads along the coast are heavily affected. At present, the men of this community have utilized their local knowledge and skills to construct this seawall. Also, the men are using cement to keep the rocks intact to provide a high degree of protection from coastal flooding and erosion.

pads.title: #Switzerlan – jet fuel that is 100% carbon-neutral
pads.snippet:
Scientists have developed a way to make carbon-neutral jet fuel for hard-to-electrify heavy transport using sunlight and air.

The fuels release as much carbon dioxide (CO2) when combusted as they absorb from the atmosphere when produced, so no additional CO2 emissions are generated.

The new process could further efforts to combat climate change by decarbonizing transport sectors like aviation, which is responsible for almost 3% of all human-made carbon dioxide emissions, shipping and road haulage.

pads.title: Local Handmade Cork Wood Jewelry

pads.title: Kizha Intregrate farm_Race Taureau
pads.snippet: kizha Intregrate farm est une ferme intégré qui vise son autonomisation à travers une agriculture et un élevage vert et durable. La maitrise de l'eau est entre autres un facteur clé dans la réussite des activités agrosylvopastoral au Niger. Dans le souci de protection de l'environnement Kizha produit ses aliments bétails dans la ferme à partir de sa production fourragère qui se fait toute l'année grâce à un système d'irrigation utilisant l’énergie solaire mais aussi le gaz. La bouse des bétails est amassée dans une fosse fumière puis utilisé pour enrichir le sol nous utilisons aussi système de mulch aucun ENGRAI CHIMIQUE n'est utilisé et très prochainement l'installation d'un système de production de biogaz qui sera utilisé par le système d'irrigation, l'installation d'une unité de transformation fruitiers les déchets issus seront aussi utiliser pour l'enrichissement du sol.  Kizha c'est la création d'emplois permanent, la sensibilisation des plus jeune dans la protection de l'enivrement à travers un agro business responsable et qui respecte l’environnement à travers une économie circulaire, Kizha se veut être une ferme complètement autonome écologique.  La promotrice de cette ferme a innové dans la sélection des races de vache au Niger. C’est qui l’a value le second prix de la BAGRI meilleurs jeunes producteurs exposants / Elevage pour un taureau croisé Race Goudali x Race Holstein de la foire nationale du Niger de l’édition 2022 (7eme édition du Sahel Niger). Ce taureau est le fruit d’une insémination artificielle avec pour « père » les semences d’un mâle de race Holstein, fournies par le Programme National d’Amélioration Génétique (PNAG) et pour « mère » une femelle de race Goudali. La race Holstein est de robe pie (noir et blanc), la race Goudali est de robe blanc-gris, mais le descendant est tout noir. L’objectif de cette insémination est d’assurer une bonne production de lait et de viande, mais aussi d’avoir des sujets aptes à la traction animale. Ce taureau est âgé de 4 ans, 10 mois. Il a un poids estimé à 864 kg et une hauteur au garrot de 1,60 m. L’animal est bien dressé, docile. Il est utilisé pour le labour et peut labourer un hectare par jou

pads.title: Puzzle Energy de Boké
pads.snippet: La solution énergétique par la fabrication d’un générateur électrique grâce à l’assemblage divers équipements et objets locaux. Cette solution énergétique est une initiative de monsieur N’Famara Touré, ingénieur   mécanique et ses collaborateurs qui ont mis en place un réseau de production et de distribution d’électrique alternative qui dessert des centaines de PME et de familles à Boké. Le dispositif est composé de d’un moteur de batteuse agricole modifié (le modèle 1115) ; d’un système de refroidissement à l’aide de deux cuves d’eau et un circuit électrique monophasée. Avec une gestion en forme de parrainage et une desserte allant de 6H du matin à 18h avec une pause de 30mn entre 16 et 17H ; de sorte à combler les 24H contre seulement 8h par la compagnie d’électricité nationale EDG. Trois quartiers couverts, un centre de santé, un marché avec plus de 800 ménages abonnés. Le coût global de l’investissement est estimé à 20 000 000 Gnf ; le tout entretenu par 15 personnes directement.

pads.title: Earth-IoT, agrotech platform for small and medium producers
pads.snippet: Earth-IoT is an agrotech platform that allows farmers to track their harvest, save on production inputs and share information with agricultural and financial advisors for easy access. Unlike other foreign companies in the sector, the platform is designed to be inclusive of small and medium-sized producers, not just large producers, being cheaper and using simpler language, in addition to allowing access to recommendations and personalized follow-up.

Done in a collaboration between UNAM, GIRA and the Clúster de Biocombustibles (Solid Biofuels Cluster). Currently registered for intellectual property at IMPI Registration Request, Exp. MX/u/2020/000262.

pads.title: Eco Personal Care Products
pads.snippet: Business caters mainly to the yachting and hotel industry by suppling environmentally friend customized personal care products such as sunscreen (which does not impact reefs), lotions, shampoos, face masks etc. Products are sold in bulk containers and the industry uses refillable plastic pouches that can be used up to 400 times before recycled in the national "we recycle" programme. Individual retail products are packaged in glass containers as much as possible. Locally sourced products include sargassum which is dried and used to make face powder, salt from the pond on Salt Island, papaya seeds (for facial scrub) and sugar cane for luffas. 25% of raw materials are locally sourced.

The design and the development of the device was made by INNOFEIT experts whereas INform’s experts developed a cloud back-end for data storage and analysis. As a result, the integrated solution is now commercialized as PureCloud. Moreover, INNOFEIT is in the process of developing a calibration laboratory for certifying the monitoring devices.

pads.title: Citizen Science on water quality motoring: "El desafío del agua"
pads.snippet: Description of citizen participation: Young people from 12 to 21 years old participated in the project for 3 days.  On the first day, they participated in online training sessions on the use of equipment and supplies provided by the project.  On the second day, an in-person meeting was held, where material for measuring physicochemical water variables was given.  On the last day, participants reflected in person about the collected results, the environmental issues impacting bodies of water, and the possibility to generate alternatives for improvement in water management.  Afterward, in a self-managed manner and together with a youth leader of the foundation, each participant uploaded the data to a section of the EarthEcho International's website, where there are more than 1.5 million records from all over the world, to share with the whole community.  Moreover, participants collaborated later with data analysis, phenomenon monitoring, and solution planning in meetings with activity coordinators of the organization EarthEcho International and the Coastal Development Institute Dr. Héctor Zaixso (National University of Patagonia San Juan Bosco [UNPSJB]).
